There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decision must now be called into question.

News.title: Arsenal’s big guns blow Lille away after the second string flop
News.content:
The Arsenal players wore black armbands to mark the passing, aged 94, of Ken Friar, the club’s life vice-president. He had served the club from 1945 to 2014 and was variously club secretary, managing director and a driving force in building the stadium in which they now play. Even Arteta, no sentimentalist, insisted on beginning his press conference with a tribute.

For Arteta’s players, there will be a much bigger test than this one in Munich next week against Bayern. Arsenal have already won in Naples but a victory at Bayern would be significant beyond that. Arsenal have won all but one of their 10 games this season – that big defeat at the Amex Stadium, almost one month ago. They clearly have another gear to go to when required although ideally, Arteta would not always have to ask it of the same players. The club have spent too much on this squad not to be able to trust the understudies.

Madueke did at least end the game with an assist. Of Saka’s understudy, Arteta said: “When you talk about players being clinical – what is clinical? Clinical sometimes means that they score one in every 500. It’s about generating volume and more actions and getting him into the good position because he will decide matches.”

No goals for Gyokeres this season and a general acceptance that the time for persevering with him has passed. It could be ever-dwindling returns for him in terms of game-time as the season goes. Coming off the bench for Lille in the second half was the unmistakable Olivier Giroud, now 40 and more than 14 years on since he signed for Arsenal from Montpellier. He was given a warm welcome by the home fans and, later, an equally warm farewell despite the Chelsea years in the interim. He was a much better player than Gyokeres in an era when Arsenal were in decline.

Guimarães had two chances in the first half. Lille’s Japan international Ayase Ueda had a goal disallowed for offside. Guimarães would have a further penalty appeal before the hour as Arteta began to consider the substitutions.

News.title: Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it
News.content:
England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

News.title: Donkey prices in Gaza skyrocket from $1,000 to $30,000
News.content:
The price of a donkey in Gaza has jumped from about $1,000 before the war to $30,000 today, according to one of the embattled enclave’s most senior vets.

The surge in the value of the pack animals is due to the virtual elimination of motorised private transport in the strip and the emergence of a small group of black marketeers who have become hugely rich trading in intercepted aid.

The donkeys, whose number has been halved in the past three years, are also now in comparatively short supply.

“It’s a little bit crazy and people keep asking me ‘are you sure about that number?’”, Dr Ahmed Thabet, a Gazan veterinary surgeon told the Telegraph.

“They say ‘do you mean $3,000?’ but I tell them ‘no’. The average price of a donkey before the war was between $1,000 and $1,200. Recently it was $20,000 and last week I witnessed one that was sold for $30,000”.

News.title: The secret to the perfect holiday in Somerset
News.content:
Somerset’s landscapes are steeped in legend, from the lush fields of “Avalon” to Cheddar Gorge and the wilds of Exmoor. Its winding, country lanes lead to secrets and natural splendour. The local food scene is flourishing, too, involving everyone from Michelin-starred chefs to foragers on the Mendip Hills and farmers selling cheddar and cider from the barn door.

Glastonbury Festival shines as the centre of the musical universe in June – but the region is becoming known for much more than this. Quiet, agrarian villages are now fashionable places to spend time – I’m often found dawdling over a lazy brunch, browsing designer ceramics and paddleboarding down river. Bruton has an internationally renowned art gallery and the county’s hip, country house hotels – from Soho House-owned Babington House to The Newt – are some of the UK’s most desirable.

What makes Somerset so exciting is that it preserves a bucolic way of life while keeping its finger firmly on the pulse.

News.title: Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle
News.content:
You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

News.title: AI cuts diagnosis for eye disease from 23 days to just 30 seconds
News.content:
Patients whose eye scans were read by an AI programme got results in 30 seconds, compared to facing an average waiting time of 23 days for results from a doctor, a study in Tanzania has shown.

Millions of people around the world have diabetic retinopathy, a condition where high blood sugar levels damage the tiny blood vessels in the retina.

It can lead to irreversible blindness if left untreated. Around a third of the 23 million people with diabetes in Africa have the complication.

In its early stages, diabetic retinopathy can have no symptoms, and the World Health Organization recommends that people living with diabetes undergo regular screening to check their eye health, so that they can be treated if necessary.

For the new study, published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers randomly assigned over 2,000 patients with diabetes visiting clinics in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions to either receive usual screening care, or to have a new type of AI-assisted screening.

Two fifths of the participants had changes in their eyes that needed referral to specialist care. In the half screened using AI, 36 per cent attended the central ophthalmology clinic within eight weeks, compared to 18 per cent in the standard care group.

Most of the people working in the regions where the study was based are farmers, said Dr Justus Rwiza of the Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre, co-author on the paper. “They depend on vision.”

The economic effects of blindness are felt by the whole family, he said, recalling how the daughter of one patient “had to stop schooling to help the mother”.

News.title: WHO probes ‘unanswered questions’ over Russian plague worker
News.content:
The World Health Organization has said it still does not have enough information to rule out a lab accident after the death of a worker in a Russian plague lab.

Last week reports emerged that Darya Shipilova, a lab worker in Irkutsk, Siberia, had died of pneumonic plague after dropping a test tube containing samples of the pathogen Yersinia pestis, which causes the disease.

Some 200 people were quarantined and there were reports of a further case. Shipilova was working at the Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East in Irkutsk.

Russian authorities have insisted that there was no lab accident and Shipilova’s mother, Svetlana, has also disputed that her daughter dropped a test tube.

“It’s impossible to break a test tube like that,” she said. “Even if you fling it at the wall. Only an amateur could say something like that,” she said.

Sports.title: Why has Scheffler been world No 1 so long and who could replace him?
Sports.content:
Scottie Scheffler continues to be the dominant world No 1 in men's golf, but how long will he stay top of the rankings and will he put more of Tiger Woods' records under threat?

Scheffler remains the most recent addition to the list of 25 players to have topped the Official World Golf Ranking (OWGR) since its introduction in 1986, with the American having four different spells at No 1 so far in his career.

The latest spell remains unbroken since May 2023, with Scheffler - as of October 12 - entering his 178th consecutive week as world No 1 and with a larger advantage over world No 2 Rory McIlroy than the Northern Irishman has over almost every active professional.

Scheffler is expected to only tee it up once more in 2026, at the Hero World Challenge from December 3-6 - an event he has finished first or second in four times over the last five years - although he already looks to have locked in starting the new year as No 1.

Image: How much longer will Scheffler stay as world No 1?

How do the rankings work and why is Scheffler so far ahead?

The world rankings run over a rolling two-year cycle, with points awarded based on the strength of that tournament's field and how high a player finishes on the leaderboard.

A golfer's world ranking then comes from dividing the number of points earned by the number of tournaments someone has played during the cycle, while bonus ranking points are given to players who have won multiple events in a 52-week period.

Image: The numbers behind Scheffler's dominant 2026 season

Scheffler registered two major wins among his six worldwide titles in 2025 and already has three victories in 2026, a campaign in which his remarkable consistency has seen him post top-three finishes in half of his 20 worldwide starts.

"He's the best player in the world by a country mile," said Sky Sports' Andrew Coltart. "It's his distance control and his ability to get scoring irons pin-high basically all the time, along with an incredible level of consistency.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day four of the Tour Championship, where Scheffler claimed FedExCup victory

"Also, very importantly, I think it's his golfing IQ and his understanding of how his game is and where his game is at - that's why he's the dominant force in the game."

How has Scheffler cemented himself as No 1?

Claiming his first three PGA Tour titles in a seven-week stretch saw Scheffler take top spot for the first time in March 2022, a fortnight before his maiden major victory at The Masters, a position he held until McIlroy overtook him that October.

Scheffler enjoyed a one-week burst back at the top after his 2023 WM Phoenix Open win and another four-week run after winning The Players the following month, before Jon Rahm leapfrogged him with his second major win secured at Augusta National.

Rahm would lose top spot when Scheffler tied-second at the PGA Championship a month later, with no player since able to end his ever-increasing reign as world No 1.

"He has managed to stay at the top for so long because he has no weaknesses across his game," Sky Sports' Nick Dougherty said. "He was once a below-average putter, but he's now world class and a top-10 putter.

Image: Scheffler led numerous statistics during the PGA Tour campaign

"The iron play is peerless - he's not just the best, he's the best by a mile when he's at his very peak. He leads birdie average and leads bogey avoidance. When you look at all of that together, there's just a reason he's better than everyone in every area."

Will Scheffler break Tiger's records?

Only Woods and Greg Norman have spent longer in their careers at world No 1 than Scheffler, who aged just 30 has already won 22 PGA Tour titles - including four majors and three legs of the career Grand Slam - and cemented his status among the greats.

Image: Scheffler's achievements are frequently compared to Woods

Woods was world No 1 for 281 consecutive weeks from June 2005 to October 2010, breaking his own record of 264 weeks previously held from August 1999 to September 2004, with Scheffler the closest to ever seriously threaten those historic runs.

Scheffler would need to remain in top spot until October 2035 to overtake Woods' career total of 683 weeks as No 1 but only until mid-October 2028 to break the longest consecutive spell, although he has plenty of work to do to reach that milestone.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' golf pundits discuss whether more American stars like Scheffler should play on the DP World Tour

"I have absolutely no valid reason why he won't [pass 281 weeks], when you look at what he's doing right now, but the level rises around you," Dougherty added. "Whether it's Rory coming back for him again or whether he has a little bit of a slump.

"Golf is just really hard to be that good for that long. Other than Tiger Woods we've never really seen it, other than Scheffler. There's new kids on the block too and they're all hungry, so I've got a feeling someone will get to him before then."

Dame Laura Davies added: "No [he won't break the record], because of the challenging pack behind him. It won't be that he necessarily drops off that much, I just think there's way too many good players just in behind him. Over two years, it's a long time."

Will Woods or McIlroy ever return to world No 1?

Woods is currently listed as 'unranked' in the OWGR standings, having not played an official event since The Open in July 2024 and only completed four 72-hole tournaments over the last six seasons.

The 50-year-old has previously ruled out a return to full-time professional golf and is unlikely to ever return to being one of the world's best, but McIlroy has continued to be Scheffler's closest challenger to the No 1 spot.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' pundits have their say on whether Rory McIlroy will ever return to world No 1

McIlroy has been no lower than third in the world rankings since Scheffler became No 1 and has been second since last March, with the Northern Irishman winning back-to-back Masters titles over the last two seasons.

"I think McIlroy still has another stint there [at No 1] because, when he's at his absolute strength, he is definitely alongside Scheffler," Dougherty insisted. "I think he can take him on his day, he just isn't as consistent as Scottie."

Coltart added: "For McIlroy to get back to world No 1 is really tough. He's at a different stage of his life and he's attained, arguably, what he ever set out in his life to attain.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Sky Sports Golf podcast discusses how much does McIlroy desire to still be one of the dominant forces in golf

"He's older, he's got different aspirations. I don't think the fire is necessarily there that it was in his belly when he was in his early 20s. It will be very difficult for Rory to do that and I hope that he proves me wrong."

Who is likely to be Scheffler's replacement?

Matt Fitzpatrick has moved to world No 3 after winning four times in 2026, although the Zurich Classic of New Orleans did not offer world ranking points, while Players champion Cameron Young and US Open winner Wyndham Clark complete the top five.

Scheffler previously jumped from world No 15 to world No 1 in a six-week burst in 2022, highlighting that rapid rises are possible, although any of his challengers would likely require multiple more victories to be next in line for the world No 1 spot.

"If it's not Rory to go past him, it's hard to imagine who it would be among this current crop," Dougherty admitted. "It could be someone like Jackson Koivun, who is a new arrival and he's a superstar that clearly stands out already.

"It could be one of these young guns, it could even be someone we don't know yet, that's going to displace him at the top of the game."

Sports.title: Billam-Smith: If Opetaia can't fight Wilder, I will!
Sports.content:
Chris Billam-Smith might set aside his pursuit of Jai Opetaia to look at other options himself.

Billam-Smith has long wanted to box Australia's Opetaia, who is widely regarded as the best cruiserweight in the world.

But Opetaia is expected to move to heavyweight to fight former world champion Deontay Wilder on the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua undercard before a potential bout with the outstanding cruiserweight David Benavidez next year.

'Willing to fight anyone'

Dana White, who promotes Opetaia, told Sky Sports: "Jai Opetaia is more than likely going to be on the undercard. [Wilder] is one that we've been talking about and working on.

Sports.title: Concern still for Labuschagne: What England learned from SA vs Aus first Test
Sports.content:
England travel to South Africa for a three-Test series starting in December, with a home Ashes on the horizon next summer, so what can they glean from Australia's 214-run win in Durban to open their own series in South Africa?

England won't get benefit of rusty-looking Proteas

It's nearly a year since the Proteas last played Test cricket - an impressive 2-0 series win in India - while this represented their first home Test since winning the World Test Championship final against Australia at Lord's in June 2025.

They looked short of a gallop, as a result.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day five of the first Test between South Africa and Australia as the visitors wrapped up a 214-run victory.

There were encouraging contributions from Aiden Markram - in particular his 237-ball, near six-hour stay at the crease in the second innings in South Africa's ultimately futile attempt to bat out for a draw - and David Bedingham, who did well with a couple of 40s at No 3.

But they weren't telling enough totals for the longer format, with South Africa guilty of throwing away numerous starts in the first innings - six players scoring at least 30 but failing to kick on - as they surrendered a 106-run deficit.

There were a couple of failures from Ryan Rickelton at the top of the order, while the captain's contribution will also be questioned as Temba Bavuma managed just four runs total across his two innings.

Image: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma failed to impact the series opener in Durban

The question is whether this was a sign of deeper problems for the side or simply the inevitable consequence of a rusty return to Test cricket after their extended absence.

England should have their answer by the time they arrive in South Africa ahead of their first Test in Johannesburg on December 17, as the hosts have two further Tests against Australia, followed by a two-match series against Bangladesh in November to get sufficiently up to speed.

Has Renshaw solved Australia's middle-order issues?

With his first-innings, career-best 190, Matt Renshaw might just have cemented himself a middle-order spot for Australia for the foreseeable future.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the first Test between South Africa and Australia, as Matt Renshaw hit a career-best 190 for the tourists.

The player of the match - who also chipped in with 82 in the second innings and a couple of wickets with his part-time off-spin - helped rescue Australia from 124-6 on day one when in danger of surrendering control of the contest amid familiar top-order batting failings.

Instead, Australia posted a score of 390 deep into day two and never looked back from there.

If Renshaw has indeed grabbed hold of the No 5 position, at least for the rest of the series, there are still questions to be resolved regarding the makeup of the rest of the batting line-up.

Travis Head, for example, had previously made that position his own before being bumped up to open midway through the Ashes last winter. It was a move that paid dividends at the time, as he hit three hundreds in winning causes at Perth, Adelaide and Sydney. However, he has not passed 22 in his three Test appearances since, including falling foul of a couple of soft dismissals in Durban.

Image: Travis Head has struggled for runs at the top of the order since smashing England to all parts last winter

Renshaw has also opened previously for Australia, so might there be a switch of the two at some point? One to revisit prior to their trip to England next summer, perhaps?

For now though, Renshaw will surely get the benefit of a run in the middle order and Australia have bigger batting issues to resolve before determining how to best use Head.

Questions remain over Labuschagne and top order

Marnus Labuschagne's wait for a 12th Test ton lives on, stretching back to July 2023.

A hundred in the warm-up match prior to the series promised much, as did his pair of 37s in this Test before failing to convert either into a score of note - let alone a century.

Averaging only 25.29 with the bat in his 24 Tests played since last topping three figures at Old Trafford in the 2023 Ashes, Labuschagne was considered incrediblly fortunate to keep his place in this Australian side but it came as a result of a lack of alternative options staking a claim.

Case and point: Nic Maddinson.

Image: Nic Maddinson registered a 33-ball duck on day one upon his return to the Australia Test team

Maddinson last played Test cricket for Australia in late 2016, averaging 6.75 across his three appearances, with his career since stalled by injury, mental health issues, and then a testicular cancer diagnosis that sidelined him for most of last year.

As a result, the 34-year-old hadn't played a first-class match since March 2025 before returning to the Test team in Durban after injuries to other batting options Cameron Green and Josh Inglis.

His first-innings 33-ball duck was an inauspicious start to his second coming in international cricket, and though he played with a great deal more freedom in the second innings, with Australia well ahead of the game by that stage - striking six fours and a couple of sixes in his 48 off 38 balls - his place in the team will continue to come under scrutiny.

Especially as Green and Inglis are now set to be back available for the second Test in Gqeberha.

To jettison Maddison after only one game back would be incredibly harsh, but Australia will be eager to get golden-boy Green, in particular, back into the team - and Renshaw has blocked his most obvious route for return at No 5.

Could he come in for Labuschagne at No 3, or Beau Webster at No 7 after he was underused as an all-rounder here? There's still much to be resolved with the look of this batting line-up.

Hazlewood and co prove they're still a force

If there was one aspect of Australia's performance that should concern England, however, it's the continued quality and depth of their bowling attack.

Image: Josh Hazlewood claimed career-best Test figures of 6-49 as Australia won by 214 runs in Durban

Josh Hazlewood's career-best Test figures of 6-49 in the second innings completed a dominant performance by the visiting seamers. Skipper Pat Cummins had led the attack first time around, taking 3-54 to help dismiss South Africa for a below-par 284 on a decent batting deck.

The evergreen talents of 38-year-old off-spinner Nathan Lyon add a further dimension, while Australia also boast Scott Boland and Michael Neser in reserve.

Image: Will Josh Hazlewood, Nathan Lyon, Mitchell Starc and Pat Cummins hang around long enough to play in another Ashes next summer?

That depth will matter over the coming months. Australia's attack is an ageing group, and the demands of an intense Test schedule - a four-match series at home to New Zealand and five away in India - following the trip to South Africa will test their fitness and durability.

How will they be holding up by the time the Ashes comes around on June 18 with the first Test at Trent Bridge?

For the time being though, any optimistic talk of Australia's attack being past their best by then looks massively premature.

South Africa team selection a head-scratcher

South Africa's team selection for the series opener raised some questions, particularly the decision to field two specialist spinners in Durban.

Image: South Africa spin twins Keshav Maharaj and Simon Harmer struggled to make an impact on the first Test

Keshav Maharaj and Simon Harmer offered a left and right-arm option, but neither proved particularly potent, with just the four wickets shared between them - including only one in the first innings, to Harmer's name, allowing Australia to recover from 124-6 to post 390.

The absence of Kagiso Rabada, having failed to recover from a hamstring injury in time for this Test, perhaps forced the selectors' hand, but it left their attack looking a little lopsided and somewhat patched together.

Wiaan Mulder, for example, should not be operating with the new ball in Test cricket.

The batting all-rounder took two wickets with it on the first morning, and burgled a couple more into day two, but was pretty ineffective otherwise for his 31 overs of hard toil through the Test.

The return of Anrich Nortje was encouraging. After an extended absence from Test cricket, the fast bowler showed glimpses of the pace and aggression that made him a major asset during his first stint in the side from 2019 to 2023.

Image: South Africa missed Kagiso Rabada in Durban and will be hoping to have him back from a hamstring injury in Gqeberha

And assuming Rabada is back fit and available for the second Test in Gqeberha, his return would provide greater balance and potency to South Africa's attack.

The prospect of Rabada, Nortje and the left-arm option of Marco Jansen steaming in would represent a much sterner challenge for Australia, and England in a couple months' time.

Sports.title: Il Est Francais makes stable debut for Skelton
Sports.content:
Ffos Las plays host to an excellent Wednesday jumps card, headlined by Il Est Francais battle with Crebilly in the feature.

4.38 Ffos Las - Il Est Francais debuts for the Skelton brigade

A host of big names arrive at Ffos Las on Wednesday, with Il Est Francais a fascinating contender in this Faucets Handicap Chase.

A dual Grade 1 winner, including the Kauto Star Novices' Chase back in 2023, he has a point to prove having been pulled up on his past three starts. The move to a new yard may spark a return to form but he will need to be at the top of his game to concede weight all round.

Jonjo and AJ O'Neill's Crebilly heads a long list of alternatives. He doubled his tally over fences when scoring at Worcester on his last outing in September and will have a fitness edge over his rivals.

Saint Segal enjoyed a successful season last year, winning on two occasions. He should appreciate the drop into handicaps having contested top-level events in the spring.

Torneo, Down Memory Lane and Southoftheborder rate each-way players.

3.30 Ffos Las - Tutti Quanti and Captain Teague clash

A brilliant field has assembled for this Listed Adept GRP Cabinets Novices' Chase, where Tutti Quanti heads four runners.

The Paul Nicholls-trained six-year-old ran out a wide-margin winner of the William Hill Hurdle in February before finishing well beaten in the Champion Hurdle. This 151-rated hurdler has long been viewed as a chaser, and he could prove a class apart on his fences debut under Sam Twiston-Davies.

Image: Tutti Quanti

Captain Teague makes his debut for Dan Skelton having switched from the Paul Nicholls yard. A Grade 1 winner as a novice hurdler, he scored on his first start over fences before suffering a setback at Newbury. Having reverted to hurdles since then, it is hoped he can get back on track in this sphere.

George's Lad dominated a decent field when winning easily at Haydock in April and makes appeal on his fencing bow, while Tamarind Bay cannot be dismissed. A winner of three of his five starts over fences, his experienced could see him go close.

2.20 Ffos Las - Sinnatra and Pourquoi Pas Papa head over fences

Sinnatra and Pourquoi Pas Papa headline an excellent line-up for this JCP Solicitors Novices' Limited Handicap Chase at 2.20pm.

Dan Skelton's Sinnatra improved with each outing over hurdles, ending the campaign with a superb second behind Storming George at Aintree. He now tackles fences on this handicap debut and this imposing type could be even better in this discipline.

Pourquoi Pas Papa looks a huge threat for Paul Nicholls and Sam Twiston-Davies. Just a four-year-old, he will receive a hefty weight allowance and having placed at the Aintree festival on his last start, he rates a smart prospect.

Light Fandango seeks a third win on the bounce having won a couple of handicap hurdles at Doncaster and Musselburgh and must be feared given a clear round.

Wandering Ego and Desertmore News complete a cracking quintet.

Best of the rest

Nocte Volatus, Ben Solo and Iron Bridge feature in the 2.55pm RWK Goodman Veterans' Handicap Chase, with the latter looking to continue where he left off after scoring at Haydock when last seen back in April.

Fresh from putting five rivals to the sword at Worcester last week, King Roly looks to go in again for Mickey Bowen in the Adept GRP Cabinets Native River Handicap Chase at 4.05pm. Here, he takes on Viroflay, who now has a mark of 144 after winning at Newton Abbot by an enormous margin last time.

The card ends with the 5.13pm Enigma Flooring Handicap Chase, with Yes Day and Jaccours the likely market principles.

Sports.title: Russell plans to take grid penalty at Las Vegas GP
Sports.content:
Mercedes' George Russell is set to take another grid penalty in November's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Russell started at the back of the grid in Sunday's Singapore Grand Prix due to a power unit change following an engine issue at the previous race in Malaysia which saw him retire late on.

He recovered to ninth but now trails Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli by 102 points in the Drivers' Championship with six rounds remaining, so is all but mathematically out of the title fight.

Prior to his Malaysia reliability woes, Mercedes had planned for Russell to take on a new power unit at the United States Grand Prix, which takes place next weekend in Austin, as they expect to have an upgrade ready, but it appears Russell will take on the new part three races later in Las Vegas on November 20-22.

Mercedes are taking up the upgrade opportunity they were granted by the FIA's ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) system to improve their engine.

The ranking of Mercedes' engine performance below Red Bull's by the sport's governing body caused some dispute, with the Milton Keynes squad arguing that the Silver Arrows, who are dominating the Constructors' Championship, already have the best power unit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell retired from the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with a power unit issue

"It will probably be later in the season now to be honest - maybe Las Vegas. But it will be there at some point," Russell told Sky Sports F1 when asked when he will take on the upgraded power unit element that will trigger a grid penalty.

"Now we have the choice to take it when we wish and we will choose slightly easier tracks [to overtake at]."

Formula 1 2026 remaining races USA October 23-25 Las Vegas November 20-22 Mexico Oct 30-Nov 1 Imola December 4-6 Brazil November 6-8

Russell: Goal is to get on top of upgrades

Russell came into 2026 as favourite for the championship with many pundits predicting Mercedes would have the best car and Antonelli, in just his second F1 season, not ready to challenge for the title. However, Russell has largely been outpaced by Antonelli with just three wins to the Italian's eight this season.

Mercedes brought an upgrade package to Malaysia which did not give them the instant performance they anticipated, so ran the pre-Malaysia car with Russell and the new upgrades with Antonelli in Singapore.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen topped every competitive session of the Sprint weekend in Singapore, although Russell was leading the Sprint race until he crashed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell crashed out shortly after taking the lead at the Singapore Grand Prix Sprint

"The goal right now is to try to improve the car. We were very much the dominant team for this whole season," said Russell.

"You look at the recent races and Red Bull have been very much best. In Baku, Max was a similar level to me. We go to Malaysia, a totally different track, and Singapore another different track, and he's dominated the last two weekends.

"Right now, the goal is to try and get on top of these updates."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Russell took over from Kimi Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore

Antonelli finished on the podium in Sunday's race after making late overtakes on McLaren's Lando Norris and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton.

The championship leader finished 25 seconds behind race-winner Max Verstappen and thinks Red Bull have done an "incredible step forward", while Mercedes are yet to extract the most from their own upgrades.

"I feel like it was a very progressive weekend, where we started off the pace and I've definitely been struggling with the new package," Antonelli said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle sat down with Antonelli to discuss his career thus far at Mercedes

"But the team did incredibly well on putting the car in a better window. And now we understand a lot more the aero package, how it works, which is very different compared to the old one. It's about trying to find the right window for the car.

"All in all, I feel like we're seeing the light at the end of the tunnel and we're going to keep pushing on this package because, also on my side, I want to help the team as much as possible in trying to understand it, also to understand which way to take for the future car as well."

Sports.title: Potter’s the present, not just the future after impressive England debut
Sports.content:
Lexi Potter could not have done more to prove she should not only be in England’s World Cup squad next summer, she could also be in the starting XI.

It's a big shout for a player that's only just broken into the England team, but her 60-minute debut against Greece couldn't have gone much better.

"It was really special," the Chelsea midfielder told ITV Sport after the game. "I am very happy and proud. It was a bit of a rush before the game and I lost my phone! I was a bit nervous but once I got on the pitch, I really enjoyed it.

"It was almost a dream come true. As a young girl, it's what you dream of, playing for your country. To make my debut and to be able to start as well is very special."

The 20-year old grew into the game at the King Power Stadium. She broke up attacks, showed her range of passing, allowed Keira Walsh, Georgia Stanway and Lauren James to shine and even had a goal disallowed.

England's next few games get gradually harder. Ukraine await in the final round of play-offs before a Nations League campaign against three teams in and around the top 20 in the world.

Potter, if trusted, can get a chance to grow into the role as an England starter while also playing in important matches.

Not many players make their debut in their first international camp under Sarina Wiegman. The fact Potter was picked to start a game shows how much she's impressing already.

"You could see that there were some nerves but that's completely normal," Wiegman told ITV Sport of her midfielder after the game in Leicester. "We kept an eye on her already and now she's a starter for Chelsea, she did really well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anton Toloui provides the three biggest takeaways from England's 5-0 victory over Greece, as the Lionesses cruised into the World Cup play-offs second round.

"In our camp, she did really well straight away. Your first start for England, that's a big moment, but you can tell the position she picks up [that she was ready]. She scored a goal that was unfortunately disallowed, but nice for her."

Keira Walsh, Potter's team-mate at Chelsea, has also become her biggest hype artist. She's been telling anyone that'll listen about the midfielder's quality and potential.

Now the Lionesses have seen it first-hand on the training pitch and in a competitive match.

Image: With Potter on the pitch, Georgia Stanway played further forward and scored for England

England can take 26 players to the World Cup, a first in the women's tournament. That means six or seven midfielders will be part of the squad.

With Walsh and Stanway certainties, it's a battle between Potter, Laura Blinkilde Brown, Erica Meg Parkinson, Ella Toone, Grace Clinton and Lucia Kendall for the other spots.

It's realistic one or two of them could be left behind. Toone and Clinton were on the outside looking in at the start of the international break before being called up as injury replacements.

All of a sudden England have a load of options in a position they were once struggling for depth.

England to face Ukraine in next round England will face Ukraine in the second round of the play-offs to secure a place at next year's World Cup.



Ukraine beat Slovakia 4-1 on aggregate to progress.



The two sides were drawn in the same qualification group, with the Lionesses winning 6-1 away before following up with a 3-0 win at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.



Ukraine will play at 'home' in the first leg, and away in the second. The ties will be played between November 26 and December 5.

Potter praise from England team-mates

Georgia Stanway to Sky Sports News: "She's a really good kid. It's so good to have her around the group. She's composed, she's calm and she appears older than what you think she is. She's come in and it's as if she's been here for a really long time."

Freya Godfrey - who also made her England debut on Tuesday - to Sky Sports News: "I can't even explain it. We were in our hotel room earlier and we were going through our camera rolls with Erica [Meg Parkinson] and I came across a picture of me and Lex from 2022 on camp.

"To then have this night with her, I couldn't be prouder of her and the season she's had. She more than deserves it. To share it with someone as special as her, I've grown up with her in the youth age groups, and talking about it gives me chills.

Image: England were 8-1 winners in aggregate against Greece in their World Cup first round play-off

"Watching her walk out and sing the national anthem, me and Erica felt really emotional and proud of her."

Jess Carter to Sky Sports News: "She's great. I remember playing with her when I was at Chelsea. It's great to see her here and in this camp, she's been excellent. She's professional and she definitely does not stand out as if she's fresh in here so I'm really happy for her."

Alessia Russo to ITV Sport: "She's been brilliant in training. You can tell that she's ready for this level. She is a great kid and wants to learn. She's got the best in learning off Keira. She looks so confident and composed."

Sports.title: Saka shines as Arsenal cruise to Champions League win over Lille
Sports.content:
Arsenal scored three goals in seven second-half minutes to beat Lille 3-0 and continue their winning start in the Champions League.

The Gunners were frustrated for an hour at the Emirates Stadium but Jurrien Timber's superb finish, lifted over the goalkeeper from Noni Madueke's pass, opened the floodgates.

Eberechi Eze added the second with the help of a slight deflection from substitute Bukayo Saka's pass, and Saka added the third himself after slick interplay with Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, who were introduced alongside him after the opening goal.

Mikel Arteta used the visit of Lille to rotate his side, making five changes from the 2-1 win over Leeds as Arsenal begin a run of eight games in 25 days, but their substitutes helped to ensure they followed up last month's win over Napoli with another victory.

The Gunners should have led earlier with Bruno Guimaraes, starting for the first time at the Emirates Stadium as an Arsenal player, and Eze missing their best chances of the first period.

But Lille's resistance was broken with Timber's opener and Davide Ancelotti's side couldn't contain the Gunners, whose substitutions underlined their strength in depth, with Saka particularly impressive before another eye-catching cameo from Max Dowman.

At the other end, Lille did not register a shot on target, although striker Olivier Giroud received a positive reception on his return to the Emirates Stadium as a substitute.

The victory continues a positive start to Arsenal's Champions League campaign, and extends their winning run in the league phase to 14 games, as last year's runners-up aim to go one better.

Analysis: Saka takes up Arteta's challenge

Arteta challenged Saka to start scoring "two or three goals per game" in his pre-match press conference. He must have been listening. He only needed six minutes to find the net after coming off the bench. And that was after providing an assist with his first touch.

"If that's the case I'm very happy and welcome it," Arteta said with a smile when asked if his comments had motivated the 25-year-old. Saka is up to four goals for the season for Arsenal and there were another two on international duty with England.

Image: Bukayo Saka celebrates with his Arsenal team-mates

His display against Lille was all the more impressive given it came after an illness, according to Arteta. "He wasn't feeling that good today and yesterday. He had a bit of an illness but was really keen to contribute. He came on and made a huge impact."

His goal, struck from around eight yards out, was one of several from close range this season and provided further evidence of him getting into more dangerous areas. It was fitting that the assist, from the right-hand side, came from Havertz, the striker with whom he has often been seen interchanging positions.

The positional fluidity is helping Saka as he tries to boost his numbers in front of goal. This was another step in the right direction.

Arteta: It was a joy to watch our goals

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta: "We had moments in the first half where we arrived into a very dangerous position with a lot of advantage.

"Our technical quality wasn't good enough to deliver moments of real threat and sustain real attacks.

"We made a change at half-time and our technical level increased.

"It was a joy to watch the goals that we scored, three different players and a number of different players participating."

On his triple substitution: "I felt that it was the right moment to do it. With the way the game was panning out, the way the opponent was behaving, we needed different kinds of players.

"But credit to the starters and the ones who came on."

Saka's European record

Saka has scored 19 goals in major European competitions for Arsenal, the outright second most of any player for the club after Thierry Henry (42).

Saka has provided nine assists in the Champions League for Arsenal, with only Henry (16) and Cesc Fabregas (14) providing more.

Arsenal have won their last 14 Champions League group stage or league phase games, keeping nine clean sheets in the process.

Ancelotti: We couldn't match their rhythm

Lille boss Davide Ancelotti:

"It's really tough. With the players they always have on the bench, they can change the rhythm of the game.

"For us it was difficult to keep up with the rhythm they put after 60 minutes.

"We have to keep the good things we did for 55 or 60 minutes.

"To come here and get a good result, you have to have many things aligned and we didn't have that.

"It's too hard on the players, the score. They didn't deserve this score."
