Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Faces Race Against Time Against Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley could be racing against time to stop Daniel Dubois in Saturday’s rematch, with his damaged nose threatening to undermine his attempt to reclaim the WBO heavyweight title.

Wardley dropped Dubois twice in the first three rounds of their May fight, proving he has the power to hurt him. He couldn’t finish the job, and Dubois’ sustained attack left him with a badly cut nose and a swollen right eye before the 11th-round stoppage.

That makes another prolonged fight a concern. Paul Smith raised the possibility of Wardley’s nose reopening after seeing him in talkSPORT’s studio this week. Simon Jordan also questioned how well it had healed, predicting an early cut. Neither view establishes what will happen on Saturday, but the first fight showed how damaging Dubois’ punches can be.

Trying to out-jab Dubois looks a difficult route for Wardley. He hasn’t shown the same powerful, ramrod jab, and following Oleksandr Usyk’s approach requires more than putting combinations together.

Usyk’s movement allowed him to step into range, land, and get away before Dubois could respond. Wardley hasn’t demonstrated that same footwork. Throwing combinations while remaining in front of Dubois would give the champion opportunities to answer.

Wardley is intelligent, though, and five months may have given him time to make meaningful changes. He doesn’t need to reproduce everything Usyk does. Moving after punching and changing angles could reduce the punishment and buy him more time to find an opening.

His clearest opportunity remains Dubois’ vulnerability when caught clean. Those two early knockdowns give Wardley a reason to believe he can end the fight before cuts or swelling restrict his vision. Chasing that finish recklessly would also expose him to the punches he needs to avoid.

Smith would accept Wardley walking away afterward.

“I’d have no problem with him if he didn’t want to fight again after this,” he told talkBOXING.

Wardley hasn’t announced retirement plans. His immediate challenge is finding a way to finish Dubois—or showing enough tactical improvement to keep that clock from running out.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Backs Canelo Alvarez Over ‘One-Dimensional’ Mbilli
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora backs Canelo Alvarez’s boxing to beat Christian Mbilli, dismissing the challenger as too one-dimensional. That prediction leaves a bigger question unanswered: whether Canelo can handle the pace without tiring against a younger fighter who keeps coming.

“Canelo has the edge in this one. Mbilli is a good fighter, a strong fighter, but for me, he’s too one-dimensional,” said Fundora to DAZN.

Fundora pointed to Mbilli’s fight with Lester Martinez to explain his doubts, saying he expected a knockout.

“We saw when he fought Lester Martinez; he kind of lost, and I expected him to knock out Lester. But he lost, and Canelo has way more boxing [skills] than that.”

Fundora is committing two classic errors here: analyzing a fighter based on past reputation rather than current reality, and constructing an entire technical case on a false premise.

First, getting the outcome of the Martinez fight wrong completely undercuts his credibility. Mbilli did not lose that fight; it was a grueling split draw where Martinez had to resort to repeated, blatant shoving just to survive the inside pressure and create punching room. Building an argument that Mbilli will fold against Canelo because he “kind of lost” collapses the moment you look at what actually happened in the ring.

Second, Fundora is talking about Canelo as if this were the 2018 or 2021 version who could slip, counter, and control the center of the ring for twelve uninterrupted rounds. That fighter is gone.

At 36, after extensive wear and tear, long stretches of inactivity, and noticeable stamina drops in the second half of fights, Canelo has become an economy puncher. He relies on explosive, low-volume bursts to bank rounds while resting on the ropes.

Mbilli is the absolute worst style for an aging champion trying to conserve energy. Mbilli does not care about taking two clean shots if it allows him to land five to the body and force a phone-booth brawl.

Against a tireless pressure fighter who refuses to let him breathe, Canelo cannot just rely on superior technique. Ring IQ only works if the legs and lungs can carry out the plan for three full minutes of every round. Fundora is picking the name and the highlight reel, completely ignoring the clock and the stylistic nightmare right in front of Canelo.

Sports.title: Team Schofield Attacks Shakur Stevenson’s Power And Reputation
Sports.content:
Floyd Schofield Jr. and his father criticized Shakur Stevenson’s punching power, opposition, and reputation, with the elder Schofield arguing that his elite billing comes from his connections to famous fighters rather than the opponents he has beaten.

“He got no power. He’s only elite by association, not by who he fought, because he haven’t fought nobody elite,” said Floyd Schofield during their Fight Hub TV interview. “People put him on the scales. Why? Because Andre Ward managed him. Because Crawford is like his big brother. Because Floyd Mayweather wanted to manage him when he was coming out the Olympics.”

Schofield’s father also called Shakur “a clown,” questioning why the boxing community gives his opinions so much attention.

The criticism followed Stevenson’s comments on X after Schofield’s unanimous decision win over Lucas Bahdi for the vacant WBA lightweight title. Shakur dismissed Schofield as a C-level fighter, something the newly crowned champion clearly hadn’t forgotten during the interview.

“When he tweeted, I was like, he really a fan because he was watching me. I can’t remember the last time I watched a Shakur fight,” said Schofield Jr.

The younger Schofield questioned Shakur’s right to criticize him after sharing the ring with a puncher like Bahdi. His complaint focused on Stevenson’s use of movement when facing dangerous opponents.

“He uses the whole ring like a track field,” said Schofield Jr. “Somebody who fights like that can’t tell me how I fight or how I should fight or what type of fighter I am.”

Schofield acknowledged that he has things to improve, yet remained pleased with his performance and the crowd’s reaction. Later, he endorsed his father’s comments: “You said everything I could say, bro. I agree 100%.”

The father’s strongest argument concerns opposition. Having Ward and Crawford’s approval doesn’t replace beating top fighters. Shakur’s power is a separate question, because a fighter can succeed through timing, accuracy, and defense without producing knockouts.

For all their criticism, the Schofields aren’t pushing to face Stevenson next. His father said their plans have nothing to do with Shakur, while discussing William Zepeda as an easier fight to arrange.

The insults are getting louder, while a fight between them remains outside Team Schofield’s immediate plans.

Sports.title: Vito Mielnicki Targets Major Step Up Against Xander Zayas
Sports.content:
Vito Mielnicki Jr. is asking for a major step up in class against Xander Zayas, calling for the fight on social media and offering to meet the former unified light middleweight champion at Madison Square Garden or in Puerto Rico.

Mielnicki’s win over Austin Williams has put him in position to pursue a bigger fight. Zayas would test whether Vito’s fairly basic style can take him much further against opponents with championship experience.

“Nothing but respect for my guy @xander.zayas, but this is the fight that needs to happen!!” Mielnicki wrote. “The big room at MSG or in Puerto Rico.”

Vito deserves credit for seeking it, especially with Puerto Rico among his proposed locations. He has been matched well and kept mostly out of harm’s way. The Williams victory was a good result, although Austin had already been softened up by defeats against Carlos Adames and Hamzah Sheeraz.

Zayas would bring quicker combinations and a more polished offensive game. This could be as high as Mielnicki goes unless he shows more versatility than he has needed through much of his career.

It’s also a good fight for the Top Rank-promoted Zayas. He has the skills to beat Vito through boxing or trading, with enough firepower to make an offensive approach worth watching.

The concern is whether Xander chooses to use it. His movement and holding against Jorge Garcia Perez and Abass Baraou produced wins without consistently showing how entertaining his offense could be. Taking that same approach against Mielnicki would be a disappointing choice against an opponent he should be able to attack.

Zayas tried boxing Jaron Ennis, found little success, and eventually traded before being stopped. Vito doesn’t present the same threat. Xander should have more opportunities to plant his feet and throw combinations without facing the punishment Ennis delivered.

Eddie Hearn has proposed interim fights for both before a summer meeting. Nothing is signed, but Mielnicki has made his interest clear. If it happens, Vito gets a chance to prove his ceiling is higher than it looks, while Zayas gets an opportunity to win with some excitement.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Accepts Keyshawn Davis Fight, Awaits Contract
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he agreed to face Keyshawn Davis more than a month ago, contradicting Davis’ claim that he only just agreed to their planned December bout. Hitchins states the paperwork has still not arrived.

Keyshawn has spent the week hyping up his plans for fight night. Hitchins insists nothing is real until promotional teams deliver actual contracts.

“I accepted this fight over a month ago still no contract or anything official I’m still waiting for a contract and time is fucking ticking Keyshawn,” Hitchins posted on X.

That timeline cuts directly into the narrative Davis presented online. Davis made it sound like Hitchins stalled before giving in. Hitchins argues the delay sits entirely with the business side.

“Buddy finally accepted the fight.. this fight in December, this sh*t personal. Africa, I’m on yo ass in December, and I’m gonna beat yo ass,” Davis said.

Trash talk builds interest, but the bout still needs signatures. Hitchins and Davis represent two of the elite talents around the welterweight limit. On pure ring ability, they sit above most rivals, which makes the pairing significant regardless of social media squabbling.

Hitchins controls range behind a stiff jab. He rarely surrenders clean targets. Opponents who charge him blindly spend full rounds eating counters from outside.

Davis brings fast hands, heavy body work, and sharp punch selection. He must apply disciplined pressure. Following Hitchins without cutting off the ring will cost him rounds on the scorecards.

The central tactical issue comes down to style. Keyshawn needs to impose his tempo. Hitchins aims to make opponents second-guess their timing and reset from distance. Both possess the technical sharpness to punish miscalculations.

Before strategy and tactics, promoters must produce the paperwork. Hitchins insists he signed off on the bout weeks ago. With December fast approaching, the matchup remains talk until the contracts land.

Both guys carry themselves like established pound-for-pound attractions, but neither draws genuine ticket sales or pay-per-view numbers on his own. Hitchins has an Olympic pedigree and slick defensive fundamentals, yet his style often alienates casual fans, and his biggest career win is a controversial nod over Gustavo Lemos. Keyshawn Davis has real offensive talent, but he is still largely living off Olympic silver medal hype.

Sports.title: Saudi Boxing Money Has To Come Down
Sports.content:
Spencer Brown sees a noticeable shift coming to Saudi boxing. Tyson Fury’s manager expects the massive purses to shrink, with fewer mega cards happening each year even though the Kingdom plans to stick around. From his perspective, the current spending pace simply cannot hold, creating a whole new reality for fighters across the sport.

“I think that the money has to go down because nobody can keep paying that sort of money,” Brown told The Ariel Helwani Show.

He made sure to dismiss rumors that Saudi investment is drying up completely. Instead, he sees Riyadh scaling back the volume of blockbuster events.

He pointed to Fury’s December 11 meeting with Anthony Joshua in Cardiff, a deal he helped put together, calling it one of the final spectacles of its kind. Moving forward, he predicts fans will see just one or two events of that size annually. While speaking as a dealmaker rather than an official spokesperson for Riyadh Season, his perspective carries genuine weight.

“I think this is one of the last of the big fights we’re going to see. I think you might get one or two big fights a year in future,” Brown said about the Fury vs. Anthony Joshua clash.

The real trouble will be convincing boxers to accept smaller checks again. Once a fighter pockets Saudi riches, traditional offers funded by gate receipts or pay-per-view sales feel like an insult. A matchup can make all the sense in the world on paper, yet stall out completely if someone insists on another monster payday.

That dynamic could trigger prolonged layoffs. Fighters risk sitting around, holding out hope for an invitation to the rare marquee card. Veterans near the end of their careers do not have time to waste on the sidelines, but the temptation of holding out for life-changing money remains strong.

A market cool-down could ultimately force promoters to build fights around realistic budgets again. For that model to succeed, fighters who want to stay active will have to adjust their financial expectations accordingly.

Fighters who grew accustomed to eight-figure guarantees for low-demand, mismatched events are going to hit a wall of stubborn inactivity before reality sets in.

Human nature and boxing economics suggest the immediate reaction won’t be humility. It will be entitlement.

When a boxer makes $10 million to $20 million fighting an unheralded opponent in an atmosphere with minimal gate pressure, that number ceases to be a windfall in their mind. It becomes their baseline. Returning to a traditional promotional model where their guarantee is tied directly to pay-per-view buys and ticket sales in London, New York, or Las Vegas feels like a drastic demotion.

The fallout is likely to split fighters into distinct groups:

First come the holdouts. The biggest names with heavy bank accounts will sit on the sidelines, convinced that their manager or promoter simply isn’t trying hard enough, or that Riyadh will eventually circle back when a headline slot opens.

They will post training clips on social media, call out other stars, demand absurd splits, and reject viable market-rate offers. Some will sit out twelve to eighteen months before grasping that the sovereign wealth subsidy has actually contracted. For aging stars, this wait will quietly run out their athletic primes.

Second comes the rude awakening for mid-tier names. Fighters who received inflated purses simply to fill out stacked undercards will discover that traditional promoters have zero appetite to subsidize them. If a fighter does not shift tickets in their home market or drive subscriptions, domestic promoters cannot afford them at Saudi rates.

These fighters will face a blunt ultimatum: accept pay cuts of 60 to 75 percent, or retire. Those who need money to maintain luxury spending habits will swallow their pride, sign realistic contracts, and return to competitive, grinding fights where they actually have to take risks.

Ultimately, the market correction will be painful. Boxing spent years living in an artificial economy where risk and commercial return were completely divorced. Once the spigot tightens, the fighters who want to stay relevant will have no choice but to get back in the gym and fight each other on realistic budgets, while the ones chasing long-gone purses will simply wait themselves into irrelevance.

Sports.title: Carlos Adames Signs With Zuffa Ahead Of WBC Deadline
Sports.content:
Carlos Adames has joined Zuffa Boxing, handing the company another 160-pound titlist along with natural pairings against Aaron McKenna and Denzel Bentley. His immediate task centers on an existing top contender who has been waiting in line.

The WBC champion must handle top-ranked Meiirim Nursultanov. Both camps face an October 20 deadline to strike a deal before purse bids get called. Switching promotional banners does nothing to erase that mandate.

“One of the most avoided men in boxing has just joined the Zuffa Boxing roster!” the promotion posted on X, citing Adames as the reigning titlist and The Ring’s top middleweight.

The official statement omitted any debut date or specific rival, leaving open how rapidly matchmakers plan to get him inside the ring.

This acquisition allows the company to pit its stable against one another. Adames taking on IBF belt holder McKenna offers an obvious starting point, assuming both men navigate their mandatory duties. It would offer McKenna a prime platform to test himself against someone marketed as the best in the weight class.

Bentley has publicly staked his claim as well. Following his agreement to box Shane Mosley Jr. on November 7, he declared that facing McKenna would crown the division leader, openly doubting if Adames or Erislandy Lara truly deserve top billing based on their track records.

Adames landing under the same roof gives Bentley a direct chance to back up his talk. Overcoming McKenna would serve as a massive victory, yet stepping in against Adames settles the debate outright rather than trusting opinions and rankings.

The roster now holds enough talent to orchestrate high-level clashes at 160 pounds. The real objective lies in turning those names into actual fights. With the WBC cut-off date arriving in seven days, Adames faces a quick choice on how to direct his championship reign.

A title unification between Adames and Bentley makes plenty of sense on paper, yet Bentley must sort out his WBO status before anyone starts drawing up contracts. Yoenli Hernandez sits in the mandatory slot, leaving officials to rule on whether Bentley can take a voluntary defense against Mosley Jr. Skipping Hernandez risks Bentley losing his hardware at the conference table, which instantly ruins the appeal of unifying later.

Bentley might slip up against Mosley Jr. this November, while Hernandez represents an even sharper tactical threat if the order gets enforced.

The real problem Zuffa faces is its middleweight stable. Collecting belts and accumulating regional contenders looks great on a corporate roster sheet, but packaging belts does not automatically manufacture marquee attractions.

Adames, Aaron McKenna, and Bentley are capable fighters, but none of them possess the crossover appeal required to anchor major pay-per-view broadcasts on their own. Callum Walsh has UFC machinery and Dana White pushing him hard in Irish-American hubs, but his ceiling remains heavily questioned by anyone paying attention to genuine top-tier opposition.

Holding sanctioning body hardware without undisputed public recognition leaves the stable vulnerable. Hardcore observers recognize Yoenli Hernandez as the absolute boogeyman at 160 pounds. His Cuban amateur pedigree, slick defensive mobility, and offensive timing make him the nightmare matchup that sanctioning bodies love to avoid mandating. Bentley or McKenna entering a ring with Hernandez would mean walking into a technical trap with minimal mainstream commercial reward and massive downside risk.

Zuffa essentially has an internal ecosystem of mid-tier titleholders who can trade belts among themselves, but as long as Hernandez sits outside that circle waiting for his shot, any claims to real division supremacy remain empty to knowledgeable fans.

Without Yoenli, Zuffa is essentially running an insulated tournament of secondary names where the belts act as promotional props rather than proof of true dominance.

You can stage Bentley versus McKenna or feed Adames to Walsh to generate domestic buzz, but knowledgeable boxing audiences see right through internal round-robins that deliberately bypass the best fighter on the planet at 160 pounds. Hernandez is the legitimizer. He provides the genuine world-class credibility that transforms a manufactured stable into an authentic division takeover.

Until Zuffa opens the checkbook to bring Hernandez into the fold or puts their titleholders in front of him, their middleweight project remains a closed shop, avoiding its true acid test.

Sports.title: Armando Resendiz Steps Into Jermall Charlo Vacancy Against Koen Mazoudier
Sports.content:
Armando Resendiz faces a tricky rebuilding spot this weekend when he steps in against Koen Mazoudier. Coming off the loss of his WBA super middleweight belt to Jaime Munguia in May, Resendiz finds himself taking over a date originally booked as a tune-up for Jermall Charlo, positioned on a low-profile card that has struggled to grab fan attention.

Resendiz (16-3, 11 KOs) takes on Mazoudier (16-4-1, 6 KOs) over ten rounds on Saturday, October 17, at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. An injury sidelined Charlo, creating an unexpected opening for the former champion on the Sebastian Fundora versus Ermal Hadribeaj undercard.

Mazoudier views the late swap as a genuine upgrade in credibility. In his eyes, taking down Resendiz carries far more weight than beating a faded name returning from another lengthy layoff.

“Beating Charlo would have come with excuses like, ‘He is old and inactive’, and all these different reasons why I’d beaten him,” Mazoudier told Fox Sports Australia.

Mazoudier makes a solid point for his own career, but the contrast is sharp for Resendiz. Dropping down from headline clashes against Caleb Plant and Munguia to face an opponent brought in to shake off Charlo’s ring rust represents a steep slide in stature. Resendiz went from pulling off a signature upset against Plant to dropping his belt, and now he is working to rebuild momentum on short notice.

The loss to Munguia stripped away plenty of momentum built from that Plant triumph. Munguia relied on steady footwork to keep Resendiz chasing throughout a flat contest, completely neutralizing the heavy pressure that troubled Plant. Resendiz fell back into the chasing pack without the kind of fire that sparks clamor for an immediate big money fight.

This matchup does not do much to alter that reality. Buzz around the event has remained quiet, with Fundora defending against Hadribeaj barely moving the needle. The Resendiz and Mazoudier clash sits even further below the radar.

A victory keeps Resendiz active, but handling Mazoudier will not instantly restore his top-tier status. He must look dominant, dictate the tempo, and deliver the kind of statement that forces people to pay attention again. Coasting to a decision over a fill-in opponent leaves him facing an uphill climb to secure elite competition down the road.

Ghana News.title: Petrol, diesel prices set to fall from Oct. 16 as LPG faces 18.5% hike
Ghana News.content:
Petrol and diesel prices are expected to fall marginally at the pumps from Friday, October 16, 2026, while liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) could see an 18.5% increase per kilogram.

This is according to the Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies’ pricing outlook for the next pricing window.

Breakdown

Petrol is projected to decline by almost 2% to GH¢17.67 per litre, while diesel could fall by 3.32% to GH¢19.30 per litre.

LPG, however, is expected to rise by 18.5% to GH¢20.60 per kilogram.

During the October 1 pricing window, most oil marketing companies maintained their prices following a GH¢2 levy on diesel and a government intervention in which Tema Oil Refinery and Sentuo Oil supplied refined products to the companies at previous prices.

Reasons for the price changes

The Chamber attributed the projected adjustments to developments on the international market and recent government subsidy measures.

In its report, the Chamber said average crude oil prices rose by 2.03% to US$126.73 per barrel for the October 16 pricing window.

It attributed the increase to renewed supply concerns, as Ukraine questioned a proposed US-backed energy ceasefire and Saudi Arabia faced fresh attacks amid the war with Iran.

Prices of refined petroleum products, however, recorded mixed movements. LPG rose by 7.77%, while diesel fell by 6.68% and petrol declined by 3.93%.

Meanwhile, the Ghana cedi depreciated by 1.61% to GH¢11.8222 to the US dollar, based on average bank rates between September 26 and October 11, 2026.

The Chamber said the cedi had lost more than 11% against the dollar so far this year, with seasonal import demand and higher energy costs continuing to put pressure on the currency.

Despite these developments, petrol and diesel prices are expected to see only modest reductions at the pumps, in line with projections from several analysts earlier this month.

NPA lowers petrol and diesel price floors

The National Petroleum Authority (NPA) has also reduced the minimum prices for petrol and diesel for the October 16 pricing window.

Market data sighted by Joy Business shows that the petrol price floor has been lowered from GH¢16.45 to GH¢16.09 per litre.

The diesel price floor has also been reduced from GH¢17.97 to GH¢17.09 per litre.

The LPG price floor, however, has increased from GH¢11.10 to GH¢13.87 per kilogram.

The NPA said these price floors exclude premiums charged by International Oil Trading Companies (IOTCs), operating margins of Bulk Import, Distribution and Export Companies (BIDECs), and margins charged by Oil Marketing Companies and LPG Marketing Companies.

Those charges will be determined independently by the respective companies in accordance with the prescribed Petroleum Products Pricing Formula.

Ghana News.title: Bank of Ghana engages stakeholders in Techiman
Ghana News.content:
The Bank of Ghana (BoG) has held a day’s stakeholder engagement forum at Techiman in the Bono East Region, to strengthen stakeholder collaboration towards deepening public understanding of the mandate of the central bank and its policy development.

The forum, the central bank said, further sought to maintain financial stability and to create value for money.

It was on the theme: “Strengthening stakeholder relations through dialogue and engagement” and attended by traditional authorities, religious leaders, traders and market women, transport unions, Small and Medium Enterprises, community banks and microfinance institutions.

The stakeholders were taken through the mandate of the BoG, as well as microfinance sector reforms, responsible borrowing and consumer protection, currency education and identification, and proper handling of banknotes among others.

Addressing the stakeholders, Mr Bernard Otabil, the Director of Communications at the BoG, said the engagement was part of the BoG nationwide drive to deepen public understanding and to strengthen the nation’s financial sector.

He explained that the engagement was designed to enable the BoG to access feedback from the public towards policy development and unlicensed financial schemes and currency abuses.

Mr Otabil emphasised that the central bank remained dedicated to the public and strengthened public trust and confidence in the Ghana cedi.

“The Cedi is not just a paper or coin, but it’s trust and we can’t formulate the best monetary policy, if the trader in Techiman market does not understand or trust the cedi,” he stated, adding: “That is why we are here, to listen, to dialogue, and to partner for financial reforms and stability.”

Mr Otabil reiterated the BoG commitment to sustaining open dialogue with stakeholders across the regions and to promote financial literacy and financial inclusion.

He urged members of the public to report suspected activities of unlicensed financial institutions to the bank.

Mr Abdulai Lawal Abubakar, the Regional Director, Sunyani office of the BoG noted that the central bank remained committed to engaging stakeholders and to gather information that would foster the development of the bank.

“Our engagement is meant to interact with and engage stakeholders to improve the total development of our operations that would enhance the BoG’s policy,” he added.

Some of the stakeholders commended the central bank, describing the engagement as an eye opener and insightful.

They expressed concern about high lending rates as well as activities of unregulated lenders and called on the BoG to do more to tackle those challenges.

Ghana News.title: PIAC unable to verify GH¢21m petroleum-funded projects in Ayawaso West
Ghana News.content:
The Public Interest and Accountability Committee (PIAC) has been unable to verify four petroleum revenue-funded projects valued at about GH¢21 million in the Ayawaso West Municipality because of inadequate information and vague project descriptions.

‎The projects could not be identified during a field inspection to assess the use of petroleum revenues between 2012 and 2024.

‎Mr Isaac Dwamena, Executive Secretary of PIAC, said the Committee had written to the Ministry of Roads and Highways three weeks before the inspection to request additional information but had not received a response by the time of the visit.

‎The inspection team, led by Nana Soglo Alloh IV, a PIAC member and Paramount Chief of the Likpe Traditional Area, identified three road projects and a Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) compound with assistance from officials of the Assembly.

‎The road projects were the surfacing of Mega Link Road at Mempeasem, valued at GH¢178,170.13; construction of a 0.45-metre U-drain along Nii Sai Road, costing GH¢130,114.85; and surfacing of Nii Sai Road, valued at GH¢131,923.65.

‎The three projects were implemented by the Ministry of Special Initiatives.

‎The team also identified a CHPS compound at Mempeasem, which received GH¢657,395.99 in 2020 and was implemented by the Ministry of Health.

‎The four projects that remained unlocated included the construction of a concrete drain at East Legon, valued at GH¢3.35 million, and emergency road rehabilitation works costing GH¢3.9 million.

‎The rehabilitation works involved the upgrading of Spintex Road and roads and culverts in the East Legon area.

‎The other projects were the resealing of selected roads in Ayawaso West and Ga Central, valued at GH¢1.5 million, and the Boundary Road and Motorway Slip Road projects, estimated at GH¢12 million.

‎The projects were attributed to the Ministry of Water Resources, Works and Housing and the Ministry of Roads and Highways as implementing agencies.

‎Mr Dwamena said the information requested from the Ministry of Roads and Highways included the names and contact details of the contractors who executed the projects.

‎“When you go to the field armed with relevant information, it positions you better to carry out the exercise and get the results you want,” he said.

‎Mr Dwamena said PIAC could not conclude that the projects did not exist because it lacked the information needed to locate them.

‎“We would not say categorically that the projects do not exist. The information that would have enabled us to find the project, we didn’t get from the Ministry of Roads and Highways,” he said.

‎At a post-inspection meeting, Mr Gordon Domayele, Municipal Coordinating Director of the Ayawaso West Municipal Assembly, said information-sharing on centrally implemented projects was necessary to improve monitoring and accountability.

‎He called on the Central Government to involve the assemblies in projects undertaken within their jurisdictions.

‎“Sometimes, when people come from the national to ask certain questions, they think that some of us are not on top of the issue. It is not our fault,” he said.

‎The inspection formed part of PIAC’s mandate to collect data from stakeholder institutions and conduct physical visits to projects funded with petroleum revenues to assess value for money and promote transparency and accountability in the management of the revenues.

Ghana News.title: Ketu North MP led delegation petitions government over deteriorating Weta Irrigation Scheme
Ghana News.content:
Eric Edem Agbana, Member of Parliament (MP) for Ketu North, has led a delegation of chiefs, rice farmers and concerned youth from Weta to petition the Ministry of Food and Agriculture for urgent rehabilitation of the deteriorating Weta Irrigation Scheme.

The petition, presented on Monday, was received on behalf of the Minister by Mr John Dumelo, Deputy Minister of Food and Agriculture, who assured the delegation of the government’s commitment to rehabilitating the scheme and supporting farmers to revive the agricultural facility.

The delegation called for immediate intervention to restore the irrigation infrastructure and reclaim farmlands severely damaged by years of operational challenges.

The farmers said more than 1,200 families had been affected by the situation and appealed for appropriate compensation to help them recover their livelihoods.

They also called for a thorough investigation into the utilisation of World Bank funds released for the redevelopment of the scheme to ensure accountability and transparency in the implementation of the project.

Mr Agbana described the scheme as a critical agricultural asset with significant potential to boost rice production, create employment and strengthen Ghana’s food security.

He said the continued deterioration of the facility had imposed considerable hardship on farmers and their families, stressing the need for urgent and decisive government intervention.

The MP assured the delegation that he would continue to engage the relevant authorities to secure concrete action towards rehabilitating the scheme and addressing the concerns of affected farmers.

He said the intervention should result in a clear rehabilitation plan, accountability for funds committed to the project and a credible strategy to restore the livelihoods of farmers.

Mr Agbana reaffirmed his commitment to ensuring that the concerns of the people of Weta remained on the national agenda until meaningful progress was achieved.

Ghana News.title: Unpaid contractor delays KATH Mother and Baby Unit as materials deteriorate
Ghana News.content:
The stalled Mother and Baby Unit project at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital (KATH) is facing further setbacks, with its consultant project manager warning that construction materials procured for the facility are deteriorating, and some have already become defective or expired due to prolonged delays.

Consultant Project Manager Emmanuel Fobi Asabere disclosed this during a visit by Parliament’s Select Committee on Health to the abandoned facility in Kumasi to assess the project’s status and challenges.

He said the contractor had been unable to resume full-scale construction because payments for work already undertaken remained outstanding, leading to repeated suspensions.

Mr Asabere said the project had been suspended for about 14 months, following an earlier period of reduced activity due to payment delays.

He explained that although the contractor had continued to maintain the site during the suspension, the prolonged inactivity was putting the procured materials and their warranty protections at risk.

“The suspension is as a result of non-payment to the contractor,” he said, adding that the contractor was awaiting payment before returning to work.

The project began in November 2019 as an effort to complete an existing hospital structure planned to accommodate about 850 beds.

However, assessments conducted after the contractor took over revealed serious structural defects.

Three other firms and the Ghana Institution of Engineers were subsequently engaged to evaluate the building, and their assessment concluded that repairing it would not be economically advisable.

The project was therefore redesigned as a 509-bed hospital, involving the demolition of the old structure and construction of a new facility.

Mr Asabere said the project initially cost GH¢188.5 million, but repeated suspensions led to additional expenses.

He put physical construction progress at approximately 56 per cent and procurement at 75 per cent, while confirming that the design work and demolition of the previous structure had been completed.

The outstanding payments, he warned, remain a major obstacle to resuming construction and completing the facility.

Ghana News.title: Kofi Adams says Ghanaians ignored warnings over World Cup visa payments
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Sports and Recreation Kofi Adams says some Ghanaians disregarded repeated warnings against paying intermediaries who promised to secure United States and Canadian visas for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, with post-tournament information suggesting that money changed hands without the Ministry’s knowledge.

He said prospective travellers had been cautioned against trusting individuals who claimed they could influence visa decisions through personal connections with government officials or members of the World Cup oversight committee.

Mr Adams urged Ghanaians seeking travel assistance to use registered travel and tour companies with clear procedures and contractual obligations.

He said some of the individuals allegedly demanded money by presenting themselves as friends of the Minister or people with access to the oversight committee.

He warned that such claims should not be treated as a guarantee of visa approval, stressing that the Ministry had not authorised individuals to collect money on its behalf to influence visa applications.

Speaking to Channel One TV on Tuesday, October 13, Mr Adams said he had issued several public warnings before the tournament.

However, information gathered afterwards indicated that some people still paid intermediaries, including individuals allegedly holding official positions.

“Before the World Cup, as Minister, on several occasions I had cause to warn Ghanaians and advise Ghanaians not to give money out to anybody in the name of going to offer you a visa to go to the US or Canada,” he said.

The comments come amid scrutiny of alleged visa facilitation arrangements involving the Ghana Tourism Authority and the National Sports Authority.

The Minority in Parliament has raised concerns over claims that some applicants were charged between US$7,000 and US$14,000 for visa assistance.

President John Dramani Mahama has directed Yaw Ampofo Ankrah to step aside as Director-General of the National Sports Authority as police investigate the allegations.

Ghana News.title: Banks to apply 20% VAT on cross-border digital payments with Ghana-issued cards
Ghana News.content:
The Commissioner-General of the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA), Anthony Sarpong.

Commercial banks are preparing to apply 20 per cent Value Added Tax (VAT) to payments for cross-border digital services and e-commerce transactions made with cards issued in Ghana, according to information gathered by Joy Business.

The banks say they are implementing a directive from the Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA). However, Joy Business has yet to establish the details of the directive or whether any banks have already begun applying the tax.

Standard Chartered Bank has notified its customers by email that it will begin applying the 20 per cent VAT to payments for cross-border digital services made with its Ghana-issued cards from October 15, 2026.

According to the bank, the move is in line with GRA requirements.

Transactions expected to be affected

Information gathered by Joy Business suggests that the tax could cover payments across the following categories. The full scope and treatment of individual services are yet to be confirmed:

Digital media and entertainment: Services such as Netflix, Spotify, Disney+, Showmax and beIN Sports. Software and software as a service: Products and subscriptions from Microsoft, Adobe, Zoom, Salesforce and Google Workspace. Cloud and hosting services: Platforms such as Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, DigitalOcean and SiteGround. Digital gaming and betting: Payments to platforms such as Steam, Blizzard, Roblox, DraftKings and Betway Ghana. Education and subscriptions: Services such as Coursera, Udemy, MasterClass and Cambridge University Press. Digital advertising: Payments for Google Ads, Meta Ads, TikTok Ads and LinkedIn advertising. Social media and communication: Paid services offered by platforms such as TikTok, LinkedIn, X and WhatsApp Business. Online travel and hospitality: Payments through platforms such as Booking.com, Agoda, Hotels.com, Uber and Bolt. Computer and IT services: Payments to providers such as Groundhog Tech and Neris Analytics. Security and VPN services: Subscriptions to services such as McAfee, NordVPN and ExpressVPN.

What it means for customers

Customers paying for affected services with debit or credit cards issued in Ghana should expect the 20 per cent VAT to be added to the amount payable.

Some commercial banks have stressed that the additional cost is a tax imposed under GRA requirements, rather than a fee introduced by the banks.

For affected transactions, customers could therefore pay the service price, the applicable VAT and any existing bank transaction charges.

Ghana News.title: Education Minister appeals to GAUA to call off strike, resume work on October 19
Ghana News.content:
Haruna Iddrisu, the Minister of Education, has appealed to the leadership of the Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) to call off their strike and allow academic activities to resume at public universities by October 19, 2026.

The Minister urged their leadership to return to the negotiation table with the Fair Wages and Salaries Commission (FWSC) to resolve the outstanding issues.

“I will issue a directive to the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission by close of the week to request public universities to reopen by October 19, 2026,” the Minister announced at a meeting with the leadership of GAUA on Monday.

He expressed the expectation that the striking workers – GAUA – would return to work by that date, subject to continued engagement on their outstanding concerns.

The Minister said the strike had already affected the reopening schedules of the University of Ghana and the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology, which had announced postponements of their reopening dates.

He expressed the hope that the universities would reopen on October 19 to enable academic work to resume and prevent further disruption to the academic calendar.

“I want to request GAUA to consider calling off the strike action for normal academic work to proceed and continue throughout all our university campuses across Ghana,” he said.

The Minister clarified that his role in the discussions was to facilitate negotiations on behalf of the Government, explaining that salary negotiations fell outside the direct mandate of the Ministry of Education.

He, however, acknowledged that the Government remained the employer of the affected workers and assured the unions that their legitimate concerns would receive priority attention.

On issues that could be addressed immediately, the Minister said the Ministry would expedite action through the GTEC to request public universities extend the retirement rollover arrangement to all senior members, in line with previous practice.

He disclosed that the Minister of Finance had issued a warrant for the payment of the one-off research allowance, adding that the relevant institutions were expected to complete the necessary administrative and payroll processes to facilitate payment.

On the issue of market premium, the Minister said the matter, including the restoration of parity, had been referred to the FWSC for further engagement with the unions.

He expressed optimism that the Commission would take the necessary action within its mandate and communicate the consequential steps required from the Ministry of Finance to address the unions’ concerns.

The Minister recalled that the Minister of Finance had committed to a negotiated 40 per cent adjustment to the market premium and non-basic allowance, saying the Government considered that matter to have made progress towards resolution.

He urged the union leaders to consult their members and reconsider the strike in the interest of students and the preservation of the academic calendar.

The Minister said the Government’s efforts to align the reopening of schools at all levels in September were intended to improve the coordination of the country’s academic calendar, stressing that further disruptions could undermine that objective.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: China and North Korea to open New Yalu River Bridge, state media reports
World.content:
The long-delayed bridge will formally open on Thursday, according to China’s state-run Xinhua news agency.

Share China and North Korea to open New Yalu River Bridge, state media reports on social media

China and North Korea will officially open the New Yalu River Bridge to traffic on Thursday, China’s state-run Xinhua news agency reports.

China completed its side of the bridge in 2014, hoping to boost trade ties. However, North Korea left its side unfinished for years as relations soured after Beijing supported United Nations sanctions over Pyongyang’s nuclear tests.

The first bridge connecting Russia and North Korea also opened earlier this month.

China-North Korea Relations

China’s exports to North Korea rose to a six-year high of $2.3bn last year, a 25 percent increase from the previous year. Chinese President Xi Jinping was welcomed in Pyongyang in June for the first time since 2019.

Since 2018, Beijing has tried to repair ties with Pyongyang, which also briefly began improving relations with Washington around the same time.

The China-North Korea relationship was forged during the Korean War. In 1961, the two countries signed the Treaty of Friendship, Cooperation and Mutual Assistance, which remains China’s only formal military alliance.

The treaty contains a mutual defence clause committing either side to assist the other if one comes under armed attack.

Although China was North Korea’s main diplomatic partner and protector for decades, relations strained after Beijing in 2017 supported tightening sanctions on Pyongyang for its nuclear weapons programme.

Analysts say North Korea’s recent growing relationship with Russia may have changed the balance of Pyongyang’s diplomatic dependence, reducing its reliance on Beijing.



North Korea and Russia signed a comprehensive strategic partnership treaty in 2024, including a mutual defence provision. Military and political ties between the two countries have grown considerably stronger, with North Korea deploying thousands of troops to fight in Russia’s war on Ukraine.

United States President Donald Trump also signalled an interest in repairing relations with Pyongyang last month, after his talks with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un abruptly ended in 2019. In his second term, Trump has floated meeting Kim again, though no official meeting has been set.

North Korea has not yet resumed issuing tourism visas to Chinese citizens, who once made up the bulk of its overseas visitors.

While North Korea’s trade with Russia largely involves military supplies, exchanges with China could arguably involve goods North Korea needs to develop its civilian economy, analysts have said.

World.title: Singapore’s economy grows more than 5 percent amid AI boom
World.content:
City-state’s GDP expands 5.4 percent in July-September quarter, according to advance government estimates.

Share Singapore’s economy grows more than 5 percent amid AI boom on social media

Singapore’s economy grew more than 5 percent in the most recent quarter, continuing an AI-fuelled boom that has made the city-state one of the fastest-growing advanced economies.

Gross domestic product (GDP) grew 5.4 percent year-on-year between July and September, down from a 6.2 percent expansion in the second quarter, according to advance government estimates released on Wednesday.

Manufacturing, which is dominated by the city-state’s semiconductor industry, grew 7.5 percent, according to the estimates from the Ministry of Trade and Industry.

Increased output in “electronics, precision engineering, transport engineering and general manufacturing clusters” drove growth, the ministry said, offsetting declines in the chemicals and biomedical sectors.

Construction, including AI-related investments such as data centres, expanded 8.8 per cent, according to the figures.

Despite the heady expansion, Singapore’s central bank left its monetary policy settings untouched in its latest announcement on Wednesday, citing expectations that AI demand will cool in 2027.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore, which manages monetary policy through currency exchange rates rather than interest rates, said it expected core inflation to average 1.5–2.0 percent in 2026.

“Global AI-driven growth is expected to ease in the latter half of next year from its current exceptional pace, while higher interest rates, amid elevated inflation in the advanced economies, would weigh on final demand growth,” the central bank said in a statement.



Singapore is a major global player in the booming chip sector, a position that has helped it weather choppy economic conditions, including the energy shock prompted by the US-Israel war on Iran.

The Southeast Asian city-state accounts for roughly 10 percent of global semiconductor output and 20 percent of semiconductor equipment production, according to government figures.

Yeow Hwee Chua, an assistant professor of economics at Nanyang Technological University, described Singapore’s economic performance as “impressive for a high-income economy, especially given the uncertain global environment”.

“The global technology investment boom has been an important driver,” Chua told Al Jazeera.

“Strong demand for electronics has supported manufacturing and related wholesale trade, illustrating how Singapore benefits from its position in global supply chains,” he said.

Singapore’s economy is expected to grow 5 percent in 2026, according to the IMF’s latest economic forecast, faster than any other advanced economy except Taiwan.

The city-state’s GDP grew 5 percent in 2025, its second straight year of growth above 5 percent – the first such streak since 2010 and 2011.

World.title: UN official says ‘window of opportunity’ for peace in DR Congo
World.content:
The envoy lauds the progress in diplomatic efforts despite the worsening security and humanitarian situation.

Share UN official says ‘window of opportunity’ for peace in DR Congo on social media

A senior United Nations official has told the Security Council there is a “window of opportunity” for peace in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, a mineral-rich region plagued by decades of conflict.

Huang Xia, the UN special envoy for the impacted Great Lakes Region, on Tuesday said that both US- and Qatar-led peace processes have achieved “notable progress”.

However, “despite this sustained diplomatic effort, the security and humanitarian situation in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has continued to worsen”, he added.

Several parties, including the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group and the Congolese army, have clashed in the territory, prompting a series of international diplomatic efforts.

Huang stressed the “urgency of seizing the window of opportunity, which is currently offered by the increased alignment of peace efforts”.

“Such a window does not remain open indefinitely,” he said.

“I therefore urge all parties to translate commitments into verifiable actions, and to place their trust in confidence built through deeds rather than through declarations.”

The Congolese government and the M23 signed a commitment towards a ceasefire in Doha in July 2025. The DRC and Rwanda also formalised a US-brokered peace deal in December in Washington, DC.

However, fighting has continued on the ground.

New talks were held in August in Switzerland, involving representatives from the United States, Qatar and the African Union.

Huang said the UN would facilitate a meeting on October 18 in Zambia’s capital, Lusaka, between the defence ministers of Burundi, the DRC, Uganda, Rwanda and Tanzania.

World.title: Israel returns 22 stolen ancient artefacts to Greece
World.content:
The cultural exchange comes amid strengthening ties between the two countries.

Israel has returned 22 ancient artefacts stolen from Greece, a cultural exchange that comes as the two countries strengthen ties.

Greek and Israeli officials did not provide details on Tuesday on how the artefacts were discovered in Israel or the circumstances surrounding their illegal removal from Greece.

The Israel Antiquities Authority’s Theft Prevention Unit had located the items, Pninat Yanay, Israel’s ambassador to Greece, said.

Greek Minister of Culture Lina Mendoni accepted the objects from the Israeli Antiquities Authority at a ceremony held at the National Archaeological Museum in Athens.

“It is the first time that Israel has returned antiquities to Greece, marking the starting point of closer cooperation between the two countries for the protection of cultural heritage,” Mendoni said.

“Every return of a cultural object to its place of origin has a broader symbolic and moral dimension.”

The collection includes 15 Attic vases, six Corinthian vases, and a bronze female statuette.

The objects are dated between 700 BC and 320 BC.

Yanay said the return of the antiquities created “the conditions for further strengthening cooperation between Greece and Israel”.

Greece-Israel relations

Greece and Israel have strengthened energy and defence ties in recent years.

In August, Israel signed a $3.5bn defence deal to build a multi-layered air defence system in Greece, called the Achilles Shield. It is the largest defence deal between the two countries, and one of the most significant export agreements in Israel’s recent history.

World.title: Ukrainian ex-officer goes on trial in Germany over Nord Stream blasts
World.content:
The trial is expected to run into February and could test Germany’s political stance on Ukraine.

Share Ukrainian ex-officer goes on trial in Germany over Nord Stream blasts on social media

A Ukrainian former military officer is standing trial in Germany, accused of organising the secret operation that blew up the Nord Stream gas pipelines in 2022 and cut Western Europe off from its biggest source of Russian natural gas.

The trial opened on Wednesday at the Hamburg Higher Regional Court and is expected to run into February next year.

It is the first public hearing of the evidence in a years-long investigation.

The defendant, a 50-year-old identified under German privacy rules only as Serhii K., is accused of leading a group of Ukrainian agents – including divers and an explosives expert – in one of the biggest infrastructure sabotage operations of modern times.

He denies any involvement and is the only person on trial.

The prosecution

Serhii K. was arrested in Italy in August 2025 and extradited to Germany that November.

Prosecutors accused him of working with other members of the military to plan the operation on behalf of unidentified Ukrainian state entities.

They allege he travelled to Germany through Poland on a forged Ukrainian passport about three weeks before the attack.

They say the group used a sailboat hired in the northern city of Rostock to reach an area near the Danish island of Bornholm, where they attached military-grade explosives with timers to the pipelines on the seabed.

German prosecutors say attacking civilian targets and destroying infrastructure in this way would amount to a war crime.

The blasts and the fallout

On September 26, 2022, Swedish seismologists detected several blasts, some 17 hours apart.



Three of the four concrete-coated steel pipelines ruptured, sending huge plumes of methane into the atmosphere.

Nord Stream 1 had supplied about half of Germany’s natural gas imports. Its twin, Nord Stream 2, was built but never opened, after Berlin cancelled approval shortly before Russia invaded Ukraine.

Moscow denied blowing up its own pipelines and had already cut supplies in response to European sanctions.

Ukraine’s government denies involvement.

Russia said on Monday it expected a “just verdict” naming the perpetrators and those who ordered the operation.

Another suspect, Vladimir Z., a trained scuba diver who prosecutors say was one of the divers on the team, was arrested in Croatia in August.

Last month, a Croatian court approved handing over the wanted man to Germany.

The Nord Stream case has strained ties between Berlin and Kyiv, even as Germany remains one of Ukraine’s strongest backers, with Russia and Ukraine still trading strikes.

World.title: Pope diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery, Vatican says
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has been diagnosed with lung cancer but had successful surgery to remove a lower lobe of his right lung, the Vatican has said in a medical bulletin.

The 71-year-old underwent a 90 minute surgery on Tuesday at Rome's Gemelli Hospital and was subsequently diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma.

"The operation was successful and there were no complications," the Vatican said. "After the operation, the Pope awoke normally and returned after a brief period of observation to his room," it added.

The lump was first detected during what the Vatican has described as "routine checks". The Pope is expected to remain in hospital for about a week.

Earlier, large crowds waited for hours outside the hospital for the Pope.

They cheered greetings and well wishes as he passed, while he waved and smiled back through the lowered back window of his car.

He was then met by staff on the hospital steps. "I'm sorry," one of them commiserated, to which the Pope gave a smile and a shrug. "We're here for you," he was assured.

In its statement, the Vatican said the whole lower lobe of the Pope's right lung was removed "to ensure the procedure was radical".

A Vatican source told Agence France-Presse news agency further tests were being carried out to see if there was any sign the cancer had spread.

It was Leo XIV himself who on Sunday announced news of his operation to the world, speaking from the balcony in St Peter's Square after delivering the traditional Angelus blessing.

He said the nodule, or growth, on his lung was "contained" and had been found "at a very early stage", but that doctors had advised him to have it removed.

World.title: Saudi man charged with planting 'sophisticated' recording device in OpenAI office
World.content:
A Saudi national has been charged with secretly planting a recording device in one of OpenAI's offices in California, federal prosecutors announced.

Abdulrahman Alfozan, who worked at the AI firm as an engineer, was charged federally with using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications.

OpenAI said it had discovered a "sophisticated recording device" hidden in their San Francisco office and alerted the FBI. The company said it used its AI models to track that it had been planted by an employee.

Prosecutors say the device, wrapped in toilet paper, was found inserted in a USB port on the back of a TV in an executive conference room.

OpenAI, the maker of the popular chatbot ChatGPT, said that it has no indication that source code, model weights or customer data were inappropriately accessed or taken in the incident. It said the employee has been fired.

According to the complaint, Alfozan "allegedly concealed a covert recording device inside his employer's executive conference room to secretly capture sensitive communications," FBI Director Kash Patel said in a statement.

Patel said that the alleged goal was to capture information about the company's AI product.

Alfozan has been working as an engineer at OpenAI since July 2025, prosecutors say.

On 30 September, OpenAI employees discovered the device - two days after prosecutors say it had been installed. The device was encrypted, prosecutors said.

OpenAI said they were able to use their AI models "to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier".

According to the FBI, the suspect used a "productivity tool" and a "chatbot" to research sensitive locations at OpenAI and how to secretly place audio equipment.

Chatbot prompts that he is alleged to have searched include "building, customizing, installing, audio recording, testing, obfuscating, and remote accessing a device", prosecutors allege.

He is also accused of using the chatbot to ask about "'build[ing] a continuous audio recorder,' 'customiz[ing] Wi-Fi . . . connectivity,' 'improv[ing] audio and live listening,' and 'encrypt[ing] the SD card'".

World.title: Germany puts Ukrainian on trial accused of blowing up Nord Stream pipelines
World.content:
The case has highlighted differences of opinion on the trial in Kyiv and Berlin.

Oleksandr Merezhko, who chairs the Foreign Affairs Committee in the Ukrainian parliament, points out that the blasts took place during a time of war with Russia and "Nord Stream 2 was nothing but a tool used by Russia in order to get prepared for the war".
