In separate testimony, a mechanic told the court that accused number four had sold him a vehicle that was later discovered to have been stolen.

All seven accused have pleaded not guilty to the charges against them.

World.title: Why AI makes computer worms harder to stop
World.content:
WASHINGTON - Anthropic's warning that AI-powered "worms" could soon spread across smart gadgets is the latest in a series of studies showing how artificial intelligence could supercharge self-spreading malware.

A computer worm is malicious software that spreads between devices on its own.

In June, Nicolas Papernot, an associate professor of electrical and computer engineering at the University of Toronto, led a team that built a prototype AI worm using freely available AI models.

Papernot, who has signed an open letter with recommendations for policymakers, spoke to AFP about why AI makes these attacks harder to stop.

The interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Q: How is AI changing these types of attacks?

A: The reality is that a lot of these "IoT" (Internet of Things or connected home) devices have very poor cybersecurity hygiene, and so they are very easy targets for bad actors to compromise.

Historically, a worm would exploit a fixed set of vulnerabilities, and that meant you could fix these vulnerabilities and prevent the worm from propagating any further to devices that had been updated.

Now, with AI, an attacker can design a worm that tailors the attack strategy to that device's specifics and these vulnerabilities can be different.

This makes it significantly harder to interrupt the propagation of an AI-driven computer worm, because you have to anticipate all the possible vulnerabilities the devices might present.

Some of these vulnerabilities are not software bugs.

They can also be misconfigurations -- for instance, if someone has used the same password for multiple services, or hasn't configured a database properly.

What AI-driven malware does is accelerate the pace at which these vulnerabilities are exploited and the scale.

In the past, your corner coffee shop, or the laptop in your basement that you use very rarely, might not be up to date, but it wouldn't be targeted by a human attacker, because they don't have the resources and the time to do that.

Now, the autonomy gained by using AI means that all these devices that are less immediate targets become interesting targets as a launchpad to attack more interesting targets.

But we have to keep in mind that a human is launching an agent.

Once launched, the agent can replicate, as we showed in our work, but it is launched by a human.

Q: What can we do to mitigate the risks?

A: We won't bring the risk to zero and we have to realise that, despite the fact that some of these vulnerability fixes are available, people don't update their devices or don't apply the fixes in a timely manner.

Despite cybersecurity experts calling for increased cybersecurity for decades, we still live in a world where a lot more can be invested in improving the security of our computer systems.

There are really three things we recommend in the very short term.

The first is to change development and testing practices to ensure that AI models are initially disconnected from the internet, as a precaution, to understand their behaviour better before we expose critical infrastructure on the internet [to them].

The second recommendation is to create an international body to standardise both how we train and how we contain AI models. Both are important. We want to train models that are safer.

The last part is about making reporting of security incidents mandatory. Right now, we are only getting information as a function of what AI developers are willing to release, and that's a big problem.

In particular, the academic community needs a lot more information about incidents to be able to develop countermeasures much more quickly.

Otherwise, we have to do a lot of research on understanding the threat first, before we can develop the countermeasures. Otherwise we won't see what bad actors are doing until an attack is launched.

World.title: Big US banks report strong earnings and stay bullish on AI
World.content:
NEW YORK - Major US banks offered a largely upbeat outlook, expressing confidence that the artificial intelligence investment boom will continue despite worries and public pushback around the technology.

JPMorgan Chase and Goldman Sachs were among the banking heavyweights reporting higher third-quarter profits due in part to solid trading and financial advisory revenues while describing continued US consumer health despite persistent inflation.

Executives face shifting challenges that include the grinding US-Iran war that has raised energy prices and recent moves by the Federal Reserve and other central banks to lift interest rates in light of inflation and rising US Treasury yields.

But perhaps the biggest question facing the industry's medium-term outlook concerns the durability of the AI boom and a growing list of public worries, most recently over the risk that rogue AI agents could harm or even destroy human life.

That is on top of other difficult questions, such as potential job losses and the impact of massive data centres on energy prices and water supplies.

Bankers acknowledged the resonance of these issues but said they saw no appreciable impact on the momentum behind the buildout.

"No one knows the exact line of travel but at its base, this technology is real," said Goldman Sachs Chief Executive David Solomon.

"Lots of things can go wrong and slow it down," said Solomon, who describes the current period as a "very strong technology super cycle."

The push behind big AI ventures is "very much still in effect," said JPMorgan Chase's Chief Financial Officer Jeremy Barnum.

"The capex is still getting spent," Barnum told a media conference call. "The deals still need to get done. People still want access to the market."

But the International Monetary Fund voiced caution Tuesday over the AI investment boom, warning of "elevated" risks with potential perils including a possible AI-related market correction.

"Weaker or less durable AI investments and profitability could be a shock that triggers a market correction," the IMF said in a report released in tandem with annual gatherings with the World Bank.

- Healthy job market -

The comments from bankers came as JPMorgan reported a six percent increase in profits from a year ago to $15.3 billion, lower than the $15.85 billion forecast by FactSet analysts.

An earnings press release pointed to $658 million in securities investment losses and a 12 percent uptick in expenses, primarily driven by higher compensation and greater spending on technology and marketing.

After huge increases in the second quarter in markets-related business, revenue growth was expected to moderate somewhat in the just-finished July-September quarter.

Barnum described consumer spending as "sort of robust" despite persistent inflation. But monetary policy decisions remain a watch item.

"The consumer is currently very healthy, primarily because of a healthy labour market," Barnum said.

"But if the central bank needs to cool things off and that involves an aggressive extended rate cycle, almost by definition, that's going to involve higher unemployment, which will produce weaker consumer credit results."

At Goldman Sachs, profits during the July-September period was $5.1 billion, up 33 percent from the year-ago level but down 20 percent from the second quarter when business conditions were especially robust.

Goldman saw muted activity in some parts of its markets business, such as fixed income, currency and commodities. But net revenue in equities trading soared 72 percent from the year-ago level.

Solomon cited recent studies that estimate the US data centre build-out as costing more than $10 trillion in investment through 2032. That prospect is a key element in what he describes as the current "top quartile" market.

While not every data centre project will move forward, "there is going to be a lot of financing to do and we're going to be in the middle of that," he said.

"It may be over time, as the financing needs growth, that there's pressure on rates and that will affect the returns and viability of certain projects."

But "one thing is clear, there's a lot of demand for compute at the moment," he said.

Among other big banks, Citigroup reported a 40 percent jump in profits to $5.2 billion, while Wells Fargo reported a 6.5 percent increase to $6.0 billion.

JPMorgan shares fell 0.9 percent while Goldman Sachs dipped 0.2 percent. Citigroup dropped 5.6 percent while Wells Fargo lost 3.1 percent.

World.title: Pope Leo has cancerous tumour removed in lung operation
World.content:
VATICAN CITY - Pope Leo XIV had a cancerous tumour removed from his right lung in a 90-minute operation on Tuesday and "woke up normally" after the procedure, the Vatican said.

A Vatican source said further tests were being carried out to determine if the cancer had spread.

"To ensure the procedure was radical, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed," the Vatican said in a statement.

The operation "confirmed the diagnosis of a pulmonary adenocarcinoma, as suspected from the pre-operative tests", it said.

The 71-year-old pope was in the operating room at Rome's Gemelli hospital for a total of three hours and the operation lasted half that time.

"The surgery was successful and there were no complications," the Vatican said, with a source adding that he had requested dinner after the procedure.

Juanita Mora, medical spokesperson for the American Lung Association, told AFP that when this type of cancer is "caught in early stages, then it has a very, very good prognosis".

She said much would depend on the stage of the cancer found and whether it had spread.

In cases of surgical removal and when the cancer is caught early and localised, five-year survival rates from lung adenocarcinoma were "80 to 98 percent", she said.

"They'll determine if he needs chemotherapy, radiation therapy, targeted therapy, or immunotherapy for the adenocarcinoma," she said.

World.title: Rayners strikes twice as Sundowns stay ahead of Pirates
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - South African striker Iqraam Rayners scored twice as Mamelodi Sundowns won 4-1 at Richards Bay on Tuesday to retain a one-point Premiership lead.

Second-placed Orlando Pirates were equally convincing winners, beating TS Galaxy 3-0 in Soweto, where another national squad striker, Tshepang Moremi, notched his fourth league goal this season.

AmaZulu stayed third, four points behind Sundowns, by edging Durban City 2-1 in a local derby and Kaizer Chiefs lie fourth after a 1-1 draw with Stellenbosch in Johannesburg.

Despite being among the most consistent scorers in domestic competitions for several seasons, Rayners often starts on the bench with Colombian Brayan Leon the preferred first choice.

But with Leon rested, Rayners took his chance to impress Portuguese coach Miguel Cardoso, heading Sundowns in front for the second time on 37 minutes.

The 30-year-old struck again just three minutes into the second half, and a volley from full-back Fawaaz Basadien completed the scoring in the 59th minute.

Midfielder Tashreeq Matthews had put Sundowns ahead after 18 minutes with a low shot and defender Lwandile Mabuya pounced on a rebound soon after to equalise.

Pirates recovered from losing a knockout competition final against Sundowns last Saturday to dominate lowly Galaxy. Boitumelo Radiopane and Simphiwe Masilela also scored for the winners.

Chiefs, seeking a first league title since 2015, drew for the fifth time in eight matches and trail Sundowns by nine points.

Both goals came in the second half with Sinoxolo Kwayiba giving Stellenbosch a 48th-minute lead that Mduduzi Shabalala cancelled 10 minutes later.

World.title: Misplaced anger? President Ruto chases 'ghosts', turns Uhuru and Sifuna into bogeymen
World.content:
For two months in a row, the Head of State has framed next year’s General Election as a contest between himself and his predecessor. [File, Standard]

An adage goes: when your house is on fire, you do not chase after fleeing rats; instead, you put out the fire. President William Ruto seems to be doing the exact opposite.

At a time when the economy is struggling, university education is paralysed, families face hunger following crop failures, and debt is choking both citizens and the government, the President appears preoccupied with political campaigns.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.

World.title: Ruto wades into growing ODM-UDA conflict
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto marks Mazingira Day by planting trees in Elgon downs, Trans-Nzoia County. [PCS]

President William Ruto delved into the growing tension among Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) and United Democratic Alliance (UDA) contenders in the Coast and asked them to tone it down during his recent tour of the region.

Speaking hours before he wound up his eight-day tour, Ruto appeared to notice the widening cracks and told politicians within the two parties to embrace a ceasefire and unite against the opposition.

The head of state, who is facing a formidable challenge from the united opposition, warned that divisions in the ODM and UDA could weaken their team, whose union gives it a chance to win the 2027 general election.

“ODM and UDA are one team, and you should accommodate each other under a broad-based government. We should not allow divisions in ODM and UDA to undermine our unity of purpose,” he stated.

His statement appeared to be directed at the growing tensions among contenders, particularly in Kwale, Mombasa and Kilifi counties where prominent politicians face challengers within the ODM and UDA political union.

President Ruto’s earlier attempt to zone the region in favour of sitting governors is also blamed for the cracks in the broad-based team at the Coast.

In Mombasa County, UDA secretary general Mr Hassan Omar has already rejected a plan by the so-called broad-based team to support governor Abdulswamd Nassir’s re-election.

Omar, who is also a member of the East African Legislative Assembly (EALA) insisted that he will challenge Mr Nassir.

Already, businessman and EALA member Mr Suleiman Shahbal has quit ODM after he left he could not get the party ticket as the president's allies favour Nassir, a deputy party leader.

Shhabal has since aligned himself to former Laikipia governor Mr Murithi Nderitu’s Kenya Reform Party even as he insisted that he will be on the ballot.

In Mombasa, Mining, Blue Economy and Maritime Affairs Cabinet Secretary Mr Hassan Joho and governor Nassir appeared to be handing over Coast which was the ODM leader late Raila Odinga’s political turf, to President Ruto.

“This region stands with Ruto because he has dignified us with title deeds and many other development projects. We however expect him to support us when we seek the presidential seat in 2032,” Joho said.

Joho’s elder brother Abubakar Joho, who is a prominent businessman, has also joined the campaign for President Ruto.

While touring Kwale, Ruto addressed the growing noise among the main contenders, Governor Fatuma Achani (UDA), Prof Hamadi Boga and Engineer Lung’anzi Chai (ODM) after the broad-based leaders appeared to settle for Ms Achani who has the backing of Sports CS and former Kwale governor Salim Mvurya.

After witnessing the rising political tension, Ruto changed tone and told the three contenders to directly seek support from the voters rather than relying on external political backing.

In a complete change of heart and political tact, Ruto emphasised that the power to choose leaders ultimately belongs to the electorate, who will evaluate candidates based on their track record and development agenda for the region.

“You should all seek votes from the people and not rely on external backing. What I need from all of you is your support,” he stated.

For long, Governor Achani has enjoyed unwavering backing of President Ruto, Mvurya and recently Joho, who had preferred Kwale to be zoned in favour of the governor and UDA.

But Prof Boga, who has been Mr Joho’s ally, described the broad-based government’s zoning arrangement as undemocratic and a coercion to the Kwale electorate who he said should be allowed to choose their leaders without external interference.

Boga has been critical about the attempt to stop some aspirants from contesting seats in the broad-based government, noting that it was possible to zone candidates and difficult to do so for the voters.

In a statement, Boga noted that former Gender CS and Kilifi governor aspirant Ms Aisha Jumwa’s recent departure from UDA to Wiper Patriotic Front (WPF) reflected a growing sense among a segment of coastal leaders that decisions about their political future are increasingly being made elsewhere, then handed down as settled outcomes rather than negotiated realities.

“Zoning at the Coast is a fantasy: You can zone candidates but you cannot zone the voters,” Boga had warned.

“And if UDA and ODM are not paying attention to that signal, they may be underestimating the political consequences of their emerging arrangements at the Coast. “There is a dangerous assumption taking root in the broad-based arrangement: that coastal politics can be settled around a table in Nairobi and then delivered to voters as a finished political package. You take this seat, we take that one, and the voters will follow,” he added.

Boga, who came second in the 2022 governor poll, warned that if the Coast is mishandled, the problem will not necessarily be that voters have suddenly embraced another political formation, but the greater danger is that voters may decide that none of the established arrangements speak for them, creating either a rebellion or apathy.

In Kilifi County, the broad-based team publicly worked with Governor Gideon Mung’aro, forcing Ms Jumwa, his main challenger, to quit the government team in protest.

Kilifi Senate aspirant Mr Stephen Kahocho and Ganze parliamentary aspirant Ms Zawadi Kingi have publicly warned that they might be forced to quit UDA and vie as independent candidates or join other political formations.

This is after it emerged that the broad-based arrangement was behind Mung’aro (ODM), Kilifi senator Stewart Madzayo (ODM) and Ganze MP Kenneth Kazungu Tungule of Pamoja African Alliance (PAA), an affiliate of UDA.

World.title: Kalonzo to Ruto: You have no numbers
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka speaks during launch of economic empowerment equipment distribution at Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos town on October 9, 2026. [John Muia, Standard]

The united opposition will deal President William Ruto a humiliating defeat in next year’s general election, Wiper Party leader Kalonzo Musyoka has predicted.

Speaking Friday in his Ukambani backyard during an empowerment equipment handover ceremony hosted by Governor Wavinya Ndeti at the Kenyatta Stadium in Machakos, Kalonzo declared the opposition will defeat Ruto at the ballot ‘no matter what magic he (Ruto) deploys.

“Ruto has been cornered. We have heard him suggesting that they will import foreigners from neighboring countries to vote for him but even so, he will not secure the numbers. We in the united opposition have committed to produce a single candidate that will face Ruto at the ballot,” Kalonzo said.

Recognizing the need to consolidate his lower Eastern vote bloc, Kalonzo rallied the Akamba community to come out in huge numbers to register as voters in the upcoming voter listing initiative by the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC).

“It is the time to redeem this country. The IEBC will as from next month undertake the final leg of voter registration and I urge all eligible voters to apply for national identity cards and register as voters,” he said, vowing he will defeat Ruto in Luo Nyanza.

Kalonzo called out Ruto over what he termed as the president’s habit of making empty promises to Kenyans. “The other day I heard Ruto promising thousands of dams across the country. He should come for benchmarking in Machakos. Retired President Mwai Kibaki and I secured African Development Bank (ADB) funding for the construction of Yatta Dam and now he has ten months left in office. When will he build?” he posed.

Former Attorney General Justin Muturi, who flanked Kalonzo, declared time was fast running out for the opposition to identify and name its presidential flag bearer for the next year’s general election.

The DP party leader, who has gone public declaring his choice of Kalonzo as the presidential ticket bearer for the opposition expressed his frustrations for the opposition’s dillydallying in naming its flag bearer.

“We (the opposition) are tired of singing one song for years that we will produce and name one person to face Ruto. When you see us here another day, do not entertain such kind of talk. Demand that it is Kalonzo for State House,” said Muturi.

During the ceremony, Governor Wavinya Ndeti unveiled assorted empowerment equipment targeting about 6000 beneficiaries across the county.

Addressing residents during the forum, Wavinya jeered at UDA-allied politicians who have been dishing out cash handouts to residents, terming it untenable.

“It is time to demonstrate to those who are approaching our people with cheap hand-outs that when the people of Machakos are given the tools to work, they produce real wealth. My commitment is that I will continue allocating resources to asset-based empowerment until every household in Machakos enjoys economic dignity,” Wavinya said.

World.title: Revealed: 84 Kenyans killed, 52 missing in Russia-Ukraine war
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi. [File,Standard]

The government has records of 354 Kenyans linked to the Russia-Ukraine war, including 84 classified as killed or missing in action and five being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine.

Prime Cabinet Secretary and Foreign and Diaspora Affairs Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi gave the updated figures in a response to Parliament on the recruitment of Kenyans into the Russian military and the detention of Kenyans in Ukraine on Thursday, October 8.

The records show that 77 Kenyans remain on the front lines, 38 are in camps, 52 have an unknown or unclassified location and 34 are hospitalised.

Another 62 Kenyans have been repatriated, while one is in detention and another has completed a military contract.

The government said Russia has stopped the enlistment of additional Kenyans after Kenya secured the country’s placement on Russia’s ‘Stop List’ during Mudavadi’s visit to Moscow in March.

“The Embassy of Kenya in Moscow has since confirmed that no additional Kenyan nationals have been enlisted in the Special Military Operation following the implementation of the Stop List,” Mudavadi said.

Russian authorities have told Kenya that requests to terminate military contracts will be considered on a case-by-case basis by individual military unit commanders.

Mudavadi said Kenya continues to engage Russian authorities and affected families over the burial, cremation or repatriation of remains after Russia said its Defence Ministry could not meet the cost of repatriating the remains of deceased Kenyans.

Five Kenyans held in Ukraine

Five Kenyan nationals are currently being held as prisoners of war in Ukraine, according to information sent to Kenya by the Ukrainian Embassy in Vienna on September 3.

The government identified them as Evans Kibet, detained since May 2025; Willi Muniu Macharia, detained since November 2025; Haron Kibet Pachenge, detained since March 2026; Joseph, detained since April 2026; and Francis Ndarua Ndungu.

Kenya’s Honorary Consul in Ukraine visited the Zakhid 1 prisoner-of-war camp and reported that the detainees were being held in humane conditions, had access to medical services and were being treated under rules governing prisoners of war.

The government also said Ukraine was holding the remains of four other Kenyans.

They are Simon Gitau, Clinton Nyapara Mogesa, Dennis Bagaka Obwori and Eric Mwangi Nyambura.

Kenya is seeking the release and repatriation of the affected Kenyans through diplomatic channels, including engagement with Ukraine and the International Committee of the Red Cross.

The government wants Kenyans held as prisoners of war to be considered as possible victims of international human trafficking.

Mudavadi said many of the affected Kenyans reported that recruiters lured them with promises of employment before they ended up in military service.

The government says the circumstances surrounding their recruitment could fit the definition of trafficking under Article 3(a) of the Protocol to Prevent, Suppress and Punish Trafficking in Persons, also known as the Palermo Protocol.

It wants the issue considered during negotiations over their repatriation so the Kenyans can access assistance available to trafficking victims.

President William Ruto has also raised the matter directly with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during a telephone conversation, according to the government.

Kenya has further received approval from Kyiv for its ambassador to Ukraine, with the government saying this will improve its ability to respond to cases involving Kenyans in the country.

The State Department for Diaspora Affairs said families should report cases to the government as soon as communication with relatives in Russia is disrupted.

Once a family reports a case, the department collects identification details, travel information and next-of-kin contacts before referring the case to the Kenyan Embassy in Moscow for verification.

The government has also facilitated the return of 62 Kenyans who had been involved in Russia’s military operations.

It has provided affected families with updates from diplomatic missions, information on compensation processes, psychosocial support and guidance on the repatriation or burial of remains.

The government said it is also expanding measures to prevent deceptive recruitment by providing pre-departure information, urging Kenyans to verify recruitment agencies and employment offers and strengthening emergency assistance through Kenyan diplomatic missions.

The scale of the recruitment first emerged publicly in February when Parliament was told that more than 1,000 Kenyans had been recruited to fight for Russia.

The National Intelligence Service report presented to lawmakers said recruiters targeted former security personnel and civilians with promises of lucrative employment, salaries and bonuses.

The figures at the time included 89 Kenyans on the frontline, 39 hospitalised, 28 missing in action, 35 in camps or bases, 30 repatriated, one detained and one who had completed a contract.

The government then stepped up diplomatic efforts. In March, Kenya announced an agreement with Russia to stop further enlistment of Kenyans into its military operations and to facilitate consular support and voluntary disengagement for Kenyans already serving.

The issue remains unresolved for many families. More than 30 families affected by the recruitment were reported this week to be seeking a meeting with President Ruto before Kenya's delegation travels to Moscow for the Russia-Africa Summit, demanding answers on missing relatives, repatriation of survivors and the return of remains.

World.title: Egypt calls on Netherlands to release detained Egyptian citizen
World.content:
Egypt’s Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty held a Monday evening phone call with his Dutch counterpart, Tom Berendsen, to discuss the release of an Egyptian citizen arrested by Dutch authorities on Sunday.

The Foreign Minister called for an explanation of the circumstances surrounding the incident and his prompt release.

During the call, Abdelatty also emphasized the critical importance of Dutch authorities providing necessary and adequate protection for the Egyptian Embassy in The Hague, in accordance with the obligations stipulated in the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.

He underscored the importance of fully honoring these obligations—consistent with the principle of reciprocity and Egypt’s firm commitment to providing necessary protection for all diplomatic missions within its territory—a stance with which the Dutch minister concurred.

The two ministers agreed to maintain consultations and resolve outstanding issues, thereby preserving the friendly relations that have united the two countries over the past decades.

World.title: Why Meta is betting its future on computers you wear on your face
World.content:
It wasn’t your typical concert experience.

I watched Billie Eilish from a perspective that felt like I wasn’t in the audience or behind the scenes, but somewhere in between: hovering near the stage alongside the singer as she grasped a fan’s hand in the front row.

This is what it’s like to watch a clip from Eilish’s 3D tour special shot in Arizona and Manchester, England, with Meta’s new VR Glasses. CNN tried the glasses at Meta’s offices in New York last week ahead of their launch in the spring. Meta is banking on experiences like Eilish’s show to make its new eyewear a hit.

Those glasses, along with camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses launching Tuesday, are part of the social media giant’s decade-long ambition to develop what it believes will be the next version of the personal computer.

Meta’s previous efforts in this space and its big bet on the metaverse have largely flopped, but the company is convinced things will be different this time. It’s betting that integration with AI agents, stylish designs and more advanced display technology will convince consumers the glasses are the future, despite widespread privacy concerns that have prompted bans and global pushback.

Using Meta’s new glasses

Meta is pitching next year’s new VR glasses as a computer, game console and movie theater in one. The glasses, which are priced at about $1,300, aren’t anything like the Quest VR headsets Meta has been selling for years, which weigh about 18 ounces and look like a visor or helmet rather than glasses.

A visitor tests Meta Quest Pro goggles at the booth of Meta Platforms at the Hanover technology Fair on April 22, 2024, in Hanover, Germany. Ronny Hartmann/AFP/Getty Images

Instead, the new version resembles a giant pair of sunglasses and weigh about 3.5 ounces. That’s because the computing components are stored in a separate module attached to the glasses with a wire.

Users interact with apps by using their eyesight as a mouse and tapping their thumb to their index finger to click. These gestures were easy to learn, although scrolling took a little practice. That involved making a fist and moving my thumb along my index finger as if it were a trackpad.

The VR glasses seem to function as a substitute for personal computers and televisions. A user can watch a movie or work across multiple displays like they normally would with their laptop or flat screen.

The goal, said Ryan Cairns, Meta’s vice president of VR, is not to replace existing computers but to expand how and where consumers can use them.

“I can put VR glasses on in the plane and basically have like three monitors’ worth of work in front of me,” he said.

CNN’s Lisa Eadicicco tries Meta’s VR glasses Lisa Eadicicco/CNN

Meta’s Ray-Ban AI glasses, on the other hand, are meant to be worn all day like normal glasses but can handle some of a smartphone’s tasks like getting directions, listening to music and answering questions.

Its newest Ray-Ban glasses don’t have a camera, excluding a controversial feature that raised widespread privacy concerns. The glasses have speakers and microphones, but Meta says the mic is limited to phone calls and talking to its AI assistant. It’s like having AirPods built into your glasses.

The idea isn’t new. Amazon has been selling Alexa-enabled smart glasses with microphones and speakers since 2019, and a wave of startups have also launched audio glasses without cameras. Meta decided two years ago that it wanted to launch audio-only AI glasses in 2026 because people frequently use their glasses for talking on the phone or listening to podcasts, said Alex Himel, Meta’s vice president of wearables.

Meta also still sells other glasses with cameras and launched an upgraded version of those spectacles last month called the Ray-Ban Meta Gen 3. The new glasses have a lighter design, a shortcut button and longer battery life, according to the company.

Meta’s quest to own the future of computing

Meta missed out on the mobile boom, ceding control of the tech devices that serve as the portal to its services to companies like Apple, Google and Samsung, thus interfering with Meta’s core advertising business. Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in 2022 that an iPhone optional setting that blocks apps from tracking users across the internet would cost the social media behemoth $10 billion in earnings that year.

Meta has spent more than a decade trying to reduce its dependence on hardware makers by releasing everything from a Facebook-branded phone to a smart home hub and VR headsets.

“There was always a very strong desire: ‘How do we have people on our own platform so we have a little bit more control?’” said Ash Saulsbury, CEO of AI company Awear, who worked in Meta’s wearables division from 2017 to 2019.

Smart glasses are gaining popularity, with shipments expected to grow 263% in the first half of 2026 and more than 7 million AI glasses sold by Ray-Ban parent EssilorLuxottica last year. But those glasses have sparked privacy concerns, and Meta’s previous hardware efforts failed to excite consumers. The company’s Reality Labs division, which includes its smart glasses and VR headsets, continues to lose money while VR headset sales have been declining industry-wide.

“The glasses are still a little bit of a solution chasing a problem,” said Daniel Newman, CEO of technology market research and advisory firm Futurum.

Smart glasses from Oakley Meta and Ray-Ban Meta in an eyewear store in Stuttgart, Germany. Christoph Schmidt/picture-alliance/dpa/AP

For Meta, there’s more at stake than just a market share of the tech products needed to operate apps.

Meta’s new hardware could give consumers more direct access to its Muse AI agent, which is key in determining how it compares with rivals like OpenAI and Google in the AI race. With glasses like the Meta Ray-Bans, users simply speak to the assistant and show it what’s in their surroundings rather than opening an app and typing a question or taking a photo.

For the VR glasses, Muse will be able to work across multiple projects and tasks managed across various virtual windows and apps, said Cairns. The glasses will ship with Muse, including support for the new Muse Wonder model announced on Monday and any other updates between now and then, he added.

Still, Meta is taking a chance that consumers are willing to add another device to their lives, especially as AI agents become more prominent in gadgets people already own. The optimistic view hinges on how much AI mirrors the smartphone boom, according to Jitesh Ubrani, who covers consumer tech for market research firm The International Data Corporation.

He compared Meta’s AI and glasses gamble to the rise of Uber or Lyft, as hailing a car ride through an app only became common with the growth of smartphones.

“Consumers essentially are just seeing AI today as a simple chatbot,” he said. “They don’t realize how powerful and capable it can be. And both AI and these glasses kind of go hand in hand right now.”

World.title: Several sailors missing after drone strike sinks merchant vessel near Bulgarian waters
World.content:
Several sailors are missing following a drone attack on a vessel off the coast of Bulgaria, according to Bulgarian officials, prompting the country’s government to summon the Russian ambassador.

Overnight there were two attacks on merchant vessels in the Black Sea, Bulgarian officials said, with one Guinea-Bissau-flagged ship, the “HS Dignity,” being sunk 15 nautical miles east of the Bulgarian village of Krapets – leading to an urgent search and rescue operation.

Another vessel called the “Chelsea 3,” which sails under the Maltese flag but is Ukrainian-owned, was struck by three drones as it sailed just 18 nautical miles off the coast of Byala, Bulgaria, leading to the emergency rescue of all 15 crew members, officials said. That crew included seven Ukrainian nationals and eight Azerbaijani nationals, who were all safely transported to the port of Varna, according to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev.

The country’s president and prime minister both strongly condemned the attacks in the vicinity of Bulgarian waters, which they indicated were likely connected to Russia.

“Bulgaria continues to seek support for an investigation into the attacks to determine the country of origin of the drones,” Radev said in a social media post on Tuesday.

“We do not have clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility to either side. However, as I have already stated, the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation,” Radev added. “I will therefore summon the Russian Ambassador for a meeting today.”

Radev added that he informed NATO allies and the European Union of the attacks, as Bulgaria seeks assistance to strengthen air and maritime surveillance and defense.

“The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable,” European Commission President Ursula von Der Leyen said in a statement, condemning the attack without explicitly mentioning Russia.

“I strongly condemn the drone attacks on merchant ships near Bulgaria’s coast,” she said. “Those responsible should be held accountable.”

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said in a statement that the alliance “will continue to work closely with our Allies in the Black Sea” and has “already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank.”

This is a developing story and will be updated.

World.title: Pope Leo in the hospital as surgery to remove growth on his lung scheduled for Tuesday
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to the hospital for surgery Tuesday to remove a small growth on his lung, in what is his first stay in hospital since the start of his pontificate.

The 71-year-old pontiff told the crowd gathered in St. Peter’s Square on Sunday that doctors had discovered a “nodule” on his lung, which he had been advised to have removed. A nodule is a mass of dense tissue that is often benign. Leo said on Sunday that the growth had been detected “at a very early stage” and was “well-contained.”

The surgery will take place Tuesday afternoon at the Agostino Gemelli University Policlinic hospital in northwest Rome, a private medical facility that has a long association with the Vatican. The hospital has a special suite of rooms for the pope on the 10th floor, which Pope John Paul II famously dubbed “Vatican three” during his frequent stays there – St. Peter’s being Vatican One and the papal residence Castel Gandolfo, Vatican two. Pope Francis also spent an extended period there early last year when he was treated for pneumonia.

The pontiff has cancelled all his public events until October 20.

“Surgeries to remove a nodule are usually minimally invasive with a low rate of complications,” said Dr. Matthew Triplette, medical director of the Lung Cancer Screening Program and specialist in pulmonary and critical care medicine. He added that patients normally stay in hospital for a few days and then continue their recovery at home.

The Vatican will continue to function while the pope is in hospital although anything requiring his signature will need to be postponed. A spokesman said Sunday that the pope will need about a week to recover following the operation.

The Vatican has no specific rules on how the leadership of the Catholic Church is transferred should the pope be incapacitated. Even if he is unconscious and undergoing surgery, the pontiff retains full papal authority.

Both Pope Francis and Pope John Paul II issued laws and statements while they were being hospitalized. Day-to-day Vatican operations are already handled by a separate team.

The pope kept his normal busy schedule Monday, holding back-to-back meetings in the morning before participating in a gathering of bishops and church leaders in the Vatican.

News of the first American pope’s surgery has led to an outpouring of well-wishes across the world, including from those visiting Rome. “We’re just hoping that his procedure is going to go well,” said Paul Kavulich, who was visiting Rome on a pilgrimage with his daughter on Monday and is from the pope’s hometown of Chicago. “And he’s got God with him – no doubt about that.”

The Vatican press office said the growth on the pope’s lung was discovered during “routine tests.” Leo is not known to have any underlying health problems, and he likes to keep active by playing tennis and going swimming.

CNN’s Antonia Mortensen contributed to this report.

World.title: UK in ‘new era of national security’ as AI supercharges rising threats, security chief warns
World.content:
London —

The United Kingdom has entered a new phase of national security as a “more contested era” replaces the stability of the post Cold War years, the head of the country’s domestic security service MI5 said Tuesday, delivering a bleak warning that a wide array of threats from states and terrorists could be supercharged by artificial intelligence.

Ken McCallum called on Britain to focus on resilience and vigilance in fending off hybrid threats directed by a triumvirate of hostile foreign states – Russia, Iran and China – as he warned the country is entering “a new era of national security.”

“These days our terrorism and state threats operational missions are pretty much of equal scale; that in itself is a huge shift across recent years,” he said in his annual speech outlining threats facing the UK.

Those threats are manifesting as “arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, coercion (and) violence,” McCallum said.

AI is “already supercharging” some of these threats, especially in cybersecurity, McCallum said as he announced the creation of a new AI Threat Assessment Center. Most worryingly, the technology also has the potential to help make destructive bioweapons, though this has not yet been realized, he added.

McCallum said one concern was that “comparatively low sophistication actors may have a capability uplift in the AI era” if governments did not enact “guardrails” around the technology effectively.

McCallum emphasized – echoing warnings from previous years – that the threat from states had continued to grow to eclipse the Cold War era. “You might be surprised to know that in 2026, MI5 is devoting more resource to countering state threats than during the Cold War,” he said. “Over the last decade, our state threats caseload has quadrupled.” He warned the new heightened threat environment was not a “temporary blip.”

Of these states, “Russia remains aggressor number one,” McCallum said, pointing to Moscow’s escalating campaign of “hybrid warfare” targeting European countries through means like a cyber attack on Polish energy infrastructure or an attempt to “use an explosive-laden drone to destroy a cargo plane in Germany.”

In the UK, “a man was charged last month under the National Security Act for allegedly preparing to sabotage a drone factory in Swindon,” McCallum added.

Still, these are not “the actions of a great power with the strategic upper hand,” McCallum said, noting that Russia’s capacity for espionage has been greatly weakened since more than 1,000 of its foreign staff have been expelled from their host countries since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Instead, Russia has scrambled “to pay criminals to do their bidding,” McCallum said.

Iran has used similar methods in an attempt to “expand their hybrid campaign,” he added. More than 50 people have been arrested in connection with Iran-linked plots, mostly directed against British Jewish communities, he said.

McCallum also referenced “Iranian ambitions to come at harder targets, like military sites,” alluding to the incident at RAF Fairford last month. He refused to provide further detail due to ongoing investigations but called the Fairford incident “not unique.”

Armed police pictured standing guard manning a roadblock at an entrance to RAF Fairford during the investigation into the incident. Justin Tallis/AFP/Getty Images

“There have been other examples, not just in the UK, but around the world,” he added.

Britain’s Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps was “almost certainly” responsible for directing a suspected plot to target the UK airbase used by US forces. Several senior Iranian officials have vehemently denied these accusations. Several men, including a British-Iranian dual national, were arrested in connection with the plot before being released on bail.

Shortly after the incident, the US made the unusual decision to move all its long-range bombers stationed in the UK back to their home bases on American soil following an unspecified new threat.

McCallum also accused China of conducting espionage in the UK, referencing an alert MI5 issued to the academic community two weeks ago and a case earlier this year which yielded the “first ever convictions for national security offences” connected to Beijing.

While he emphasized the increasing role of states, he noted that terrorism “remains a top concern for MI5” and that an “attack is highly likely.”

World.title: PM: Egypt Forum 2026 to discuss inflation-linked cash subsidies, social protection reform
World.content:
Egypt Forum 2026 will discuss ways to improve the transition from in-kind subsidies to cash support, including linking subsidy values to price movements and inflation rates to protect beneficiaries’ purchasing power, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said on Monday, October 12, 2026 .

The proposed measures aim to promote social justice and give citizens greater freedom to choose goods according to their actual needs, Madbouly said during a meeting to review the agenda of a session titled “A More Effective Social Protection System.”

The meeting was held as part of preparations for Egypt Forum 2026, scheduled to take place in the New Capital from October 19 to 24. It was attended by Social Solidarity Minister Maya Morsy, Supply and Internal Trade Minister Sherif Farouk, National Organization for Social Insurance Chairman Gamal Awad, Assistant Finance Minister for the General Budget Ali el-Sisi, and officials from relevant ministries.

Madbouly said the meeting was the second workshop to review the planned session, which will examine government efforts to support various segments of society, particularly the most vulnerable and low-income groups.

He stressed that the discussions aim to listen carefully to citizens’ concerns and public opinion on an issue closely tied to their daily lives.

The government is committed to transparency and openness, Madbouly said, adding that the discussions would address challenges encountered in the social protection sector in recent years, as well as its objectives for the next phase.

The aim is to develop outcomes that can guide government decisions and help improve services provided to citizens, ultimately enhancing their quality of life and living conditions, he added.

World.title: Government plans to position Egypt as regional tourism hub, FM says in Bangkok
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty outlined the government’s plans to position Egypt as a regional tourism hub by developing airports, modernizing its air transport fleet and expanding connectivity with international markets.

Abdelatty made the remarks during a meeting on Monday, October 12, 2026, in Bangkok with William Heinecke, Chairman of Thailand-based Minor International, one of the Asia-Pacific region’s largest hospitality and restaurant groups, to discuss ways to expand the company’s investments in Egypt, particularly in tourism and hospitality, amid promising opportunities in the Egyptian market.

Abdelatty expressed Egypt’s interest in working with the company to develop vocational and technical training programs and prepare qualified Egyptian personnel for jobs in the hotel and tourism sectors. Such cooperation would help meet growing workforce needs, attract more tourists, particularly from Asian markets, and enhance the competitiveness of Egypt as a tourist destination in line with international standards, he said.

The Foreign Minister welcomed Minor International’s plans to expand its presence in Egypt, highlighting a partnership agreement signed with an Egyptian company in October 2025 in the presence of the prime minister, as well as the launch of a residential and hotel units project on the Red Sea coast.

Abdelatty reaffirmed the Egyptian government’s support for such investment partnerships and expressed hope that the company would diversify its investment portfolio in Egypt and extend cooperation to other tourist destinations.

He also highlighted investment opportunities arising from Egypt’s development of new cities, particularly the New Capital and New Alamein City.

World.title: Egypt, UNESCO discuss expanding cooperation in inclusive sport, youth empowerment
World.content:
Minister of Youth and Sports Gohar Nabil met on Monday, October 12, 2026, with Paul Koster, UNESCO Regional Director for Cairo and director of the UN agency’s liaison office to the Arab League, as they discussed ways to strengthen cooperation in several priority areas, particularly sport for development, social inclusion, youth empowerment and digital skills development.

The meeting comes as the Ministry of Youth and Sports seeks to strengthen its international partnerships and leverage available expertise and resources to support Egyptian youth, develop sport practice and reinforce the role of sport in human development and sustainable development.

The talks explored opportunities to build on the existing cooperation between the ministry and UNESCO and develop joint programs and initiatives that use sport as a tool for sustainable development, promote community participation and expand access to sports and youth activities, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals and Egypt’s priorities for investing in people and building young people’s capacities.

Nabil stressed that his ministry attaches great importance to cooperation with international organizations and benefiting from their expertise in developing youth and sportive programs and initiatives.

Such cooperation will help broaden participation in sport, strengthen sport’s contribution to community development and promote the values of participation, tolerance and equal opportunities, he said.

He highlighted the importance of building on existing cooperation with UNESCO and developing joint projects with tangible impact, particularly in inclusive sport, empowering persons with disabilities, developing youth skills and supporting digital innovation.

He also stressed the need to align proposed initiatives with young people’s actual needs and establish clear mechanisms for implementation and follow-up.

For his part, Koster underscored the importance of strengthening cooperation with the Ministry of Youth and Sports in areas that expand opportunities for young people to participate in development and use sport to promote social inclusion and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals.

World.title: Liberia: Glassco Demands Halt to Nimba United’s Second Division Admission Over Conflict-of-Interest Concerns
World.content:
MONROVIA — Senior Professional Sisters FC President Emmett Stages Glassco has called on the Liberia Football Association (LFA) to suspend the admission of Nimba United into the Second Division League, raising serious conflict-of-interest concerns involving the club’s owner, LFA Second Vice President Adolphus Dolo.

By Jaheim T. Tumu | [email protected]

Glassco warned that admitting the club through an administrative process rather than sporting promotion threatens to undermine the credibility of football governance in Liberia, given Dolo’s position within the executive body overseeing the competition.



“No individual should be above the rules, and no football club should enjoy preferential treatment because of its association with those in authority,” Glassco declared during a press conference in Monrovia.

The controversy stems from the LFA’s decision to expand the Second Division League by admitting two additional clubs through an administrative application process—bypassing the conventional pathway of earning promotion on the pitch.

While the LFA framed the expansion as an effort to broaden national participation, Glassco argued that incorporating a club linked to a sitting senior official compromises transparency, accountability, and administrative independence.

“Can a senior official of a football governing body have a direct interest in a club seeking special administrative admission into a higher division without creating a serious conflict-of-interest concern?” Glassco asked.

Governance Questions Surrounding Dolo’s Dual Role

At the heart of Glassco’s objection is the operational conflict between Dolo’s leadership duties at the LFA and his financial interest in a club applying for entry into a league managed by the same authority.

While stopping short of accusing Dolo of outright corruption, Glassco emphasized that the potential for bias demands immediate scrutiny.

“I am not suggesting that Dolo has personally manipulated the process, nor am I presenting an allegation of misconduct as an established fact,” Glassco clarified. “Nevertheless, his dual position as a senior LFA official and an interested party creates a legitimate concern that cannot simply be ignored.”

He stressed that safeguarding public confidence requires the LFA to enforce institutional safeguards preventing both actual and perceived influence.

“Where an official occupies a senior position within the same institution administering a process from which his club stands to benefit, there must be adequate safeguards against influence,” he added.

Nimba United’s Relegation and Promotion Defeat

The dispute has drawn renewed scrutiny to Nimba United’s recent decline across Liberia’s domestic football structure.

Nimba United was initially relegated from the First Division following a points-deduction penalty for fielding an ineligible player.

The team suffered further setbacks during the 2022/23 campaign before dropping out of the Second Division entirely.

After spending two seasons outside the national league system, the club sought to regain its slot on the field in June 2026 but fell short, losing 3-2 to Bain United FC in the promotion playoff final.

“A club should never gain an advantage because its owner or controlling official occupies a senior position within the governing institution,” Glassco insisted, advocating for strict adherence to merit-based advancement.

Calls for Disclosure and Independent Review

Glassco has challenged the LFA executive board to publicly detail how the expansion process was conducted and clarify what ethical protocols were implemented.

Specifically, Glassco demands that the LFA disclose, Whether Vice President Dolo formally declared his interest in Nimba United. or Whether Dolo recused himself from board discussions and decisions regarding league expansion.

Also he wants the explicit evaluation criteria used to select administrative applicants, along with the identities of the panel members.

“The issue is not only whether his club meets the basic requirements,” Glassco asserted. “The issue is whether the process is sufficiently independent to guarantee that his position could not influence the outcome.”

Glassco urged the LFA leadership to suspend Nimba United’s admission pending a full, independent review to restore trust among member clubs and stakeholders.

“This matter is bigger than one club, one individual, or one league season,” Glassco said. “It concerns the fundamental principles upon which football governance in Liberia should operate.”

The LFA has not yet issued an official response to Glassco’s demands.

World.title: Liberia: Gbeisay’s Call to Abolish Jury Trials Sparks Constitutional Showdown, Raises Fears of Concentrating Justice in Judges’ Hands
World.content:
MONROVIA — Liberia’s top judge has declared that the country’s trial jury system has been so badly compromised that it may no longer be worth keeping. That position has set the Judiciary against the legal profession and a sitting senator, and has raised the question of what protects a verdict once the jury is gone.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

Chief Justice Yamie Quiqui Gbeisay Sr. made the call on Monday at the opening of the Supreme Court’s October Term. He told the courtroom that jury manipulation was eroding the administration of justice in both civil and criminal matters. “A corrupt jury is worse than no jury at all,” he said.



Within hours, the proposal had drawn a response from the Liberia National Bar Association (LNBA), a challenge from Senator Darius Dillon, and warnings from lawyers who say the plan would trade one weakness for another.

The Chief Justice’s Evidence

Gbeisay did not present the call as theory. He pointed to reported cases of jury tampering in Nimba, Grand Gedeh, Bomi and Margibi counties, involving charges ranging from rape to drug trafficking. He also referred to suspected interference in proceedings at Criminal Court “C” in Monrovia.

The earliest example dates to 2022 in the Eighth Judicial Circuit in Nimba County. The Chief Justice alleged that a deputy marshal assigned to the circuit had been used as a conduit to compromise a jury.

In Republic of Liberia v. David Nagbe, a rape trial in Grand Gedeh County during the May Term of 2025, tampering was reportedly identified four days after an acquittal. In Republic of Liberia v. George Bongar, another rape case, this time in Bomi County during the May Term of 2026, alleged tampering surfaced 19 days after an acquittal.

In Margibi County, he cited the drug case Republic of Liberia v. Quita Dolo et al., in which interference was reportedly suspected while proceedings were still pending.

He also discussed a US$100,000 drug-related case before Criminal Court “C” and a separate matter in which allegations of jury tampering and misconduct emerged seven days after an acquittal. According to the address, Judge Ousman F. Fieka investigated the latter and established gross jury tampering.

The Chief Justice also noted that jurors are members of the public, not Judiciary employees, but that their conduct nonetheless reflects on the courts.

The Bar Says Fix It First

The LNBA responded the same day. Its President, Cllr. Juah Lawson, condemned jury tampering and said anyone who corrupts a juror, attempts to, or serves as an intermediary strike at the integrity of the justice system. “Such conduct must have consequences,” he said.

The Bar stopped short of backing abolition. Lawson accepted the Chief Justice’s invitation for the Legislature, the International Bar, the Law Reform Commission and other stakeholders to examine the proposal and pursue constitutional reform, but drew a line around what that acceptance means. “The LNBA accepts the invitation to participate in this intervention,” he said. “However, our participation should not be understood as an endorsement of abolition.”

Lawson said trial by jury holds an important place in Liberia’s constitutional framework and argued for diagnosis before surgery. “Before we contemplate abandoning the institution itself, we should carefully examine why there is failure in particular instances and whether those failures may be corrected,” he said.

The Association listed areas it wants examined first:

– how jurors are selected and vetted;

– jurors’ security and sequestration;

– their compensation and conditions of service;

– access to jurors and their intermediaries;

– the protection of juror information;

– the role of court personnel; and

– the investigation and prosecution of those behind tampering.

“Liberia must have this conversation,” Lawson said, “but it must be a conversation grounded in evidence, constitutional fidelity and broad stakeholder consultation.”

Analysts who spoke to FrontPage Africa said the response shows the legal profession is willing to consider structural change but wants proof that stronger safeguards and enforcement cannot solve the problem.

Senator Dillon: A Referendum, not a Bill

Senator Dillon took the sharpest position. In a Facebook statement, he rejected the proposal and argued that trial by jury is a constitutionally protected right that cannot be removed through ordinary legislation. Citing Article 20(a) of the 1986 Constitution, he said abolition would require a national referendum.

He also argued that the reported cases point to weak enforcement, not a flawed institution. “We cannot simply seek to undo laws because of our failure to summon the courage to implement and enforce the laws,” Dillon wrote.

His reading of the amendment process is a statement of his own legal position, and the correct procedure would ultimately have to be settled by authoritative legal interpretation. But the constitutional text gives his argument weight. Article 20(a) guarantees due process and a fair hearing, while Article 21(h) provides for the right to a speedy, public and impartial trial by jury of the vicinity in the criminal cases it covers. Any move to abolish or substantially alter that right would call for close analysis of the applicable amendment procedures.

Who Watches the Judge?

The sharpest objection to the proposal is not about juries at all. It concerns what replaces them. A lawyer who spoke to FrontPage Africa on condition of anonymity, citing fear of retribution, strongly opposed abolition. The lawyer argued that handing greater decision-making power to judges, without addressing alleged corruption on the bench, could damage public confidence further.

The lawyer alleged that some judicial officers accept bribes to influence judgments, and that some legal practitioners will not take a case unless clients provide money meant to influence jurors. These claims are serious and have not been independently established. But they point to a possible chain of corruption in which several actors exploit the same weak points.

Critics say this is the accountability gap in the Chief Justice’s plan. Removing jurors eliminates one point of manipulation, but it does not eliminate bribery or intimidation. Someone determined to obtain an unlawful outcome could simply redirect the pressure. Instead of approaching several jurors, that person could focus on the single officer deciding the case.

That does not mean judges are generally corrupt, and nothing in the debate establishes that they are. It means that concentrating a verdict in one set of hands raises the stakes on every safeguard around those hands.

Legal systems worldwide operate judge-only trials fairly, but those systems typically rest on independent courts, transparent processes and credible discipline of misconduct. Liberia’s critics ask whether those foundations are in place. If jurors can be bought, they say, the country must also be able to say what happens when a judge is accused of being bought.

Allegations Are Not Findings

Observers also say the details of the cited cases matter. An allegation raised after an acquittal is not proof that a verdict was improperly obtained, and misconduct in one trial does not necessarily mean the whole system cannot function fairly.

What the public still lacks, they say, is a clear account of which allegations were formally investigated, what evidence was found, whether anyone was charged or disciplined, and whether those findings held up in court. Only Judge Fieka’s inquiry was described in the address as having established tampering.

That information would help separate substantiated corruption from suspicion. It would also show whether the failure lay in the jury system or in the enforcement that should have protected it. Without it, critics say, citizens are being asked to give up a constitutional safeguard before getting a full explanation of why existing laws failed.

Enforcement and Its Gaps

Many of those opposing abolition return to the same point: the law already requires protection of jury proceedings. When a juror is bribed, a court official facilitates tampering or a lawyer tries to influence a verdict, the response should be investigation and prosecution where evidence supports charges, along with professional discipline where it applies.

A credible deterrent depends on misconduct being detected, fairly investigated and punished. When it goes unpunished, scrapping the institution can look like a faster fix than confronting the people responsible. But critics argue that redesigning an institution cannot substitute for enforcement.

The same standard, they say, must apply to judges and lawyers. Allegations should be examined through independent and credible procedures consistent with due process. Judicial officers should not be presumed guilty because rumors circulate, but the authority of the bench should not shield anyone from legitimate scrutiny either.

The Judiciary’s credibility, they add, depends not only on the judgments it delivers but on how it responds when its own processes are questioned.

Questions Any Reform Must Answer

If Liberia moves toward a judge-only model, the questions critics want answered are concrete:

– How are complaints of judicial misconduct investigated, and by whom?

– What disciplinary tools exist, and how transparent are their outcomes?

– Are court proceedings documented well enough to permit meaningful scrutiny?

– What protection exists for those who report corruption inside the legal profession?

These questions, they say, go to the legitimacy of whichever system the country chooses.

Neither model is inherently better. Professional judges may be better placed to explain the legal reasoning behind a verdict, while citizen participation can guard against concentrated state power. The question, observers say, is which arrangement can protect constitutional rights and deliver impartial justice under Liberia’s actual institutional conditions.

The Chief Justice’s invitation to the Legislature, the Bar and the Law Reform Commission offers a chance to move beyond competing declarations. Those following the debate say a credible review should:

– examine the cases cited in the address and establish the status of each investigation and prosecution;

– determine how the alleged interference occurred and whether existing laws were enforced;

– assess the vulnerability of judges and court officials to improper influence, and the effectiveness of discipline;

– consider remedies such as stronger juror screening and protection, tighter security around deliberations, stricter controls on contact with jurors, better reporting channels and more effective bribery investigations; and

– weigh every proposal against constitutional requirements, defendants’ and victims’ rights, the need for timely trials and the courts’ practical capacity.

If a judge-only system is ultimately considered, they say, its backers must explain how judicial independence would be protected, how allegations against judges would be investigated, and how pending and future cases would be handled under the constitutional process required for change.

A reform of this size, they argue, should not be driven by frustration with a series of troubling cases. It should rest on evidence of which arrangements are failing, why, and how the alternative would fix them.

The Question That Remains

No one in the debate disputes that jury tampering, if proven, is a grave offense. A verdict obtained through bribery or intimidation harms defendants, victims and public trust in the rule of law.

But the Chief Justice’s critics maintain that removing juries would not resolve the underlying problem. If the jury system is compromised, they say, it must be repaired. If judges face allegations, those must be investigated fairly and independently. If lawyers are implicated, professional accountability must follow where the evidence supports it.

“No institution should be beyond scrutiny,” as critics put it, and no constitutional right should be set aside without a legally sound and publicly examined justification.

For now, the proposal has opened a debate that reaches well beyond courtroom procedure. Remove the jury, critics say, and the judge becomes even more central to the verdict. Until Liberia can say who holds the judge accountable, the question of whether the country is confronting corruption or only moving the power to decide justice from one place to another will stay unanswered.
