Executives from Volaris and Viva (formerly Viva Aerobus) say the self-styled “merger of equals” will respect brand identities and “strive to ensure consumers recognize the individual service models with which they have become familiar.”

The CNA will reportedly require Grupo Más Vuelos to meet specific benchmarks and consumer protection criteria — such as keeping fares low and avoiding widespread layoffs — according to three of the sources cited by Reuters.

Critics have raised regulatory concerns, such as route eliminations — the two companies currently operate 55 identical routes — and diminished market competition. They also point out that the transaction would concentrate 73% of domestic air traffic in a single company.

CNA approval is likely to come with requirements that the conglomerate maintain existing route networks and comply with a low-cost mandate that is aligned with regional budget operators.

Yucatán Magazine reported that the federal government has apparently sought to influence the vetting process, since both airlines “serve as redirection points and primary operators at the state-run Felipe Angeles International Airport on the periphery of Mexico City.”

While the merger, first announced last December and approved by international regulatory authorities last month, aims to increase low-cost air travel and connectivity, media reports suggest it is also a “defensive decision.”

Both carriers have experienced financial troubles since the COVID-19 pandemic. Volaris recorded a net loss of US $103.8 million in 2025 and reported a loss of US $127 million in this year’s second quarter. Viva accumulated US $133 million in losses during the first half of 2026).

According to the business consultancy Antitrust Intelligence, the merger aims to build a competitive advantage centered on cost reductions, fleet efficiencies and balance sheet recovery.

Despite the economic challenges the two airlines have been facing, market analysts and investors are said to view future operational synergies favorably.

With reports from Reuters, Yucatán Magazine and Mexico Business News

World.title: Morelos authorities free alleged criminal leader to secure release of 3 kidnapped police
World.content:
Authorities in Morelos freed an alleged criminal leader just hours after he was captured on Monday to secure the release of three kidnapped police officers.

José David Vergara, an alleged leader of the Pueblos Unidos criminal group, was detained on Monday afternoon on drug possession charges in Totolapan, a municipality in northeastern Morelos on the border with México state.

#Estados | Quema de vehículos y bloqueos carreteros se registran la tarde de este lunes en Totoloapan, Morelos, luego de un enfrentamiento armado entre elementos de seguridad e integrantes de un grupo del crimen organizado. De acuerdo con información preliminar, los hechos de violencia son resultado del despliegue de un operativo para capturar a un líder criminal considerado generador de violencia en la región. Información en desarrollo. 📹 Especial — La Silla Rota (@lasillarota) October 13, 2026

The Morelos Attorney General’s Office (FGE) said in a statement that police detained Vergara, known as “El Güero Gym,” during an anti-extortion operation. It said that “cells” of the Pueblos Unidos criminal group retaliated by detaining “three collaborators of the Eastern Region Prosecutor’s Office” — i.e., state police officers. Those officers were conducting homicide investigations and were not involved in the operation during which Vergara was captured.

After the police were kidnapped, “the protocol for handling kidnapping cases was activated to prioritize the lives of the victims being held against their will,” the FGE said before disclosing that the officers were freed at about 7:35 p.m. Monday after “the person detained hours earlier” was handed over.

“One of our colleagues was hospitalized due to a gunshot wound,” the FGE said, adding that he was in “stable” condition.

“The Attorney General’s Office of the State of Morelos stresses that the lives of our personnel are a priority for the institution and for that reason the necessary actions to protect their physical safety were carried out,” the FGE said, adding that “these criminal acts won’t go unpunished.” The newspaper Reforma reported that criminals threatened to kill the state police officers if “El Güero Gym” wasn’t released. On Tuesday, Morelos Attorney General Fernando Blumenkron Escobar said that the events in Totolapan on Monday “can’t be analyzed in an isolated way or reduced to the assertion that [organized] crime forced authorities to give in.” He said that Vergara was under investigation prior to his arrest, but was not subject to an arrest warrant. Blumenkron said the suspect was arrested for drug possession — not for high-impact crimes (such as murder) for which he is under investigation. Blumenkron also said that “at least 10 people” would be investigated in connection with the kidnapping of the three state police officers.

The capture and subsequent release of Vergara was reminiscent of the capture and release of Ovidio Guzmán López in Culiacán, Sinaloa, in 2019. The capture of Guzmán López, a drug trafficker and son of convicted drug lord Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán Loera, triggered a hostile response from the Sinaloa Cartel, leading authorities to decide to release him in an attempt to quell the violence in the Sinaloa capital. García Harfuch: Decision to release suspect was to ‘save lives’ At President Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference, Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said that the Morelos government’s decision to release Vergara was aimed at “avoiding a greater confrontation” with criminals. “In effect, it was to save lives,” he said. “There were a lot of civilian people in the streets,” García Harfuch said. Citing “preliminary information” from the Morelos government, the security minister said that the state police operation in Morelos on Monday wasn’t specifically aimed at capturing Vergara. However, when officers saw “this individual in flagrante,” they detained him, García Harfuch said. “It wasn’t an operation specifically to detain this person,” he said. As a result, state police officers had “insufficient” force and backup from federal officers to effectively respond to the violence that ensued, García Harfuch said. He said that the decision to release Vergara doesn’t mean that he will go unpunished. “We’re going to arrest him,” García Harfuch said. Vergara’s arrest triggers narcobloqueos in Morelos

In addition to kidnapping three police officers, the Pueblos Unidos criminal group responded to Vergara’s arrest by setting vehicles and tires on fire to create so-called narcobloqueos (narco-blockades).

Reforma reported that narcobloqueos were set up in four municipalities in Morelos: Yecapixtla, Atlatlahucan, Tlayacapan and Oaxtepec.

Criminals also exchanged gunfire with police officers after the arrest of Vergara. Citing “unofficial information,” the El Universal newspaper reported that at least two police officers suffered gunshot wounds.

Morelos, which borders Mexico City, México state, Puebla and Guerrero, is one of Mexico’s most violent states. It recorded 673 homicides in the first nine months of 2026, according to data presented at Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference.

4 police officers killed in crash while responding to unrest

A police vehicle in which several officers were traveling crashed on the La Pera–Cuautla highway on Monday as they headed to assist colleagues responding to the unrest that followed Vergara’s arrest.

Two officers were killed at the scene of the crash, while two of three injured officers died while being transported to hospital, according to the Morelos Security Ministry.

With reports from EFE, El Universal, Reforma and El Financiero

World.title: In a first, 2 longtime searchers for missing relatives — mother and daughter — earn official certification
World.content:
After years of searching for missing loved ones, Ceci Flores and her daughter have obtained government certification recognizing their skills, a first for relatives confronting Mexico’s disappearance crisis.

Flores announced last week that she and her daughter, Milagros de Jesús Valenzuela Flores, had received the credentials, issued by Mexico’s National Council for Standardization and Certification of Labor Competencies, an agency affiliated with the Education Ministry.

The certification recognizes expertise developed by families who search for missing relatives while pressing authorities to investigate their disappearances.

Flores, 53, has become a leading voice for Mexico’s searching families since her son Alejandro disappeared in 2015. She later founded Madres Buscadoras de Sonora (Searching Mothers of Sonora) and was named to the BBC’s list of 100 inspiring and influential women in 2022.

Alejandro remains missing, but in March, searchers recovered the remains of another son, Marco Antonio, who disappeared in 2019. DNA testing confirmed his identity earlier this year.

Flores’ daughter, Milagros, leads Jóvenes Buscadores de Sonora, a youth search collective she helped establish with about 15 other young people. She is in her mid-20s.

Mexico had 130,381 people still missing or unlocated as of Oct. 12, according to National Registry of Missing and Unlocated Persons figures reported this week by Conexión Migrante. The total excludes people already located alive or dead by that date.

The credentials fall under Competency Standard EC1542, which evaluates information gathering, preparation of case files, interviews, field and remote searches, and reporting.

Flores credited Guanajuato’s State Training Institute and the forensic and legal consulting firm Forensic and Legal with supporting the training, evaluation and certification, El País reported.

“We want to have more tools to do what no mother should have to learn to do: search for her children,” Flores wrote in an Oct. 7 post on X.

Eight women searching in Guanajuato will also receive certification after meeting the same standard, UnoTV reported last week. The women, who will receive their certificates within two months, UnoTV said, completed nine five-hour training sessions, with state scholarships covering certification costs.

In her post, Flores stressed that certification does not transfer the authorities’ search responsibilities to families or search collectives.

Mexico has about 200 such groups — who look for missing relatives while pressing authorities to investigate their disappearances — according to an Amnesty International estimate cited by ADN40 in March.

Meanwhile, Mexico City’s Cuauhtémoc borough has named its council chamber Madres Buscadoras, or Searching Mothers, according to an agreement published Tuesday in the Official Gazette.

The designation honors mothers and other searching relatives without endorsing any specific organization or political position.

With reports from El País, Aristegui Noticias, Vanguardia and Excélsior

World.title: 4 Mexican bars are among this year’s World’s 50 Best
World.content:
Mexico is home to four of the best bars in the world, according to the 2026 edition of The World’s 50 Best Bars, with two of them ranking in the top 10.

Here are the Mexican bars that made the list.

h

Handshake Speakeasy – Mexico City (No. 6)

Crowned The World’s Best Bar in 2024, Handshake Speakeasy has maintained its high global ranking thanks to its culinary approach to mixology.

Located in the heart of Mexico City’s Zona Rosa, the establishment was founded by Rodrigo Urraca, Marcos Di Battista, and Dutch bartender Eric van Beek, who is responsible for its creative cocktail program.

“Hands down, the legend of Handshake Speakeasy speaks for itself,” The 50 Best Bars said, highlighting the bar’s special take on the classic piña colada.

Bar Mauro – Mexico City (No. 10)

Located in the Roma Norte neighborhood, Bar Mauro secured 10th place and won the Disaronno Highest New Entry Award 2026, which honors the highest-ranking of the bars that enter the top 50 for the first time.

The project belongs to brothers Ricardo and Eduardo Nava and opened its doors in November 2024. Ranking even higher (No. 2) on The 50 Best Bars in North America list, Bar Mauro marks one of the standout venues in Mexico.

The 50 Best Bars highlights the Negroni (named after an Italian count), the basilico (a basil-based cocktail) and the Maurito (a diminutive of the bar’s name) as some of the bar’s most recommended cocktails.

El Gallo Altanero – Guadalajara (No. 28)

The only Mexican bar outside Mexico City to make the top 50, El Gallo Altanero is located in the city’s hip Colonia Americana neighborhood. It was opened in 2018 by Swedish bartender Freddy Andreasson and Alejandra Aguinaga.

Its cocktail menu prioritizes Mexico’s seasonal ingredients, and The 50 Best highlights the Jalisco Old Fashioned and the tuna negra (that’s the Spanish word tuna, by the way, as in the fruit of the nopal cactus).

Tlecan – Mexico City (No. 47)

This mezcalería opened in 2019, founded by Bernardo Serna, Eduardo Panchur and Eli Martínez Bello. Like Bar Mauro, it’s located in the bar-rich Roma Norte neighborhood.

Tlecan’s cocktail menu is a nod to Mexico’s agave culture and lesser-known spirits like bacanora, pox and raicilla. The 50 Best highlights the paloma blanca, made with clarified grapefruit juice, and a piña colada variation using pulque.

Beyond the 50 Best

Mexico’s presence doesn’t end with those four names. The extended list features Form + Matter (No. 59) and Licorería Limantour (No. 63) in Mexico City; and Arca in Tulum (No. 67).

Mexico News Daily

World.title: MND Local BCS: Historic ‘Cabo to Cabo’ running of the Baja 1000 announced for November
World.content:
Before the recent announcement by SCORE (Southern California Off-Road Enthusiasts) International, the sanctioning and governing body of the world’s longest-running and most legendary off-road race, that the Baja 1000 would feature a unique “Cabo to Cabo” routing for its 59th edition this November, Cabo — shorthand for either the municipality of Los Cabos or its most populous city, Cabo San Lucas — had been included on the course map on only two previous occasions: in 2000 and 2007, when the race started in Ensenada and concluded in Cabo San Lucas.

That makes this year’s race — scheduled for Nov. 9 to 15 — a historic one, and not just because the race will start for the first time in Los Cabos; specifically, on Avenida Centenario in San José del Cabo, where the 964.66-mile competition sponsored by BF Goodrich Tires will both start and finish. This will also mark the first time the Baja 1000 has been run entirely within the state of Baja California Sur.

The course map for 2026

An estimated 250 teams representing 15 countries are expected to participate in the 2026 Baja 1000. Teams (generally two drivers or a driver and navigator, along with support crew) compete across several classes determined by age and vehicle type — from trucks, cars and buggies to motorcycles, quads and UTVs — vying not only for cash prizes, but also coveted points in the SCORE World Desert Championship, for which the Baja 1000 is the season’s finale.

The Baja 1000 has no set route. Ensenada has hosted the starting line for 49 of the 58 previous races, and the finish line for 31; hence, the city’s nickname as the “Desert Racing Capital of the World.” La Paz, Baja California Sur’s capital, has also been a popular terminus, serving as the finish line 22 times.

However, new and “innovative” routes are regularly included in the course rotation.

Going ‘Transpeninsular’

“Every three years, we aim to hold a ‘Transpeninsular’ version,” notes Juan Tintos Funcke, General Manager of Score International, per El Imparcial. “The most recent one was in 2023 and ran from south to north. Normally, the route goes from Ensenada to La Paz, but that year it went from La Paz to Ensenada. That is how we constantly seek innovation and offer different challenges in our races — we adjust the logistics to keep the events appealing.”

The “Cabo to Cabo” route in 2026 will certainly be that, winding its way up the East Cape from San José del Cabo, passing La Paz and then Loreto before making a turn to head back down the Pacific Coast, skirting Todos Santos and El Pescadero on the return loop to San José del Cabo.

In total, four of the five municipalities in Baja California Sur will see action along the race route (Comondú, La Paz, Loreto and Los Cabos are included; Mulegé is not).

The birth of the Baja 1000 and its enduring popularity

Southern California hot rod pioneer Don Francisco and race vehicle builder Bill Stroppe were key links between Mexico’s legendary Carrera Panamericana — the world’s longest and most dangerous race held lengthwise across Mexico between 1950 and 1954 — and the Baja 1000. Francisco had helped Stroppe and Clay Smith prepare Lincolns for the Carrera Panamericana, experience with epic-scale routing that no doubt came in handy when he aerially surveyed the inaugural route for the Baja 1000, which was run under the auspices of NORRA (National Off-Road Racing Association), founded by Ed Pearlman, Francisco and others in 1966. NORRA organized the first six Baja 1000 races between 1967 and 1972.

Although the Carrera Panamericana supplied the precedent for an internationally promoted, grand-scale Mexican endurance race, the Baja 1000 grew directly from the timed record runs of the 1960s … inspired by the 1962 durability demonstration of Honda CL72 Scrambler motorcycles, which Dave Ekins and Bill Robertson Jr. drove from Tijuana to La Paz, navigating a network of dirt tracks, washes and trails in just under 40 hours. The 950 miles they traversed were very close to the total later covered by the Baja 1000, and 40 hours is still the time limit for teams to complete the race.

Baja’s timeless off-road allure

The challenges of the Baja California peninsula’s rugged terrain have been attracting those thirsty for adventure ever since, first from those seeking to beat Ekins and Robertson’s time, and later, during the six-decade heyday of the Baja 1000, from everyone from professional drivers to rock stars (Ted Nugent) and Hollywood movie stars like Steve McQueen, James Garner and Paul Newman (who also became a professional race car driver and completed his last Baja 1000 just before he turned 80).

Parnelli Jones, who famously described the Baja 1000 as a “24-hour plane crash,” was among the first of the crossover auto racing stars to embrace the event. After winning the Indianapolis 500 in 1963, he claimed overall Baja 1000 titles in 1971 and 1972 in his famed Dick Russell and Stroppe-built Ford Bronco, “Big Oly.” A host of Formula 1, NASCAR and IndyCar champions followed, including Robby Gordon, Jimmie Johnson, Rick Mears and Alexander Rossi.

However, following the OPEC Oil Crisis in 1973, NORRA’s permits were revoked, and the Baja Sports Committee organized that year’s race before the 1974 event was canceled, and the Mickey Thompson-founded SCORE took over in 1975 — an association that to date has lasted more than 50 years.

What’s at stake this year?

The Baja 1000 brings with it tangible economic benefits: about US $35 million is expected to flow to municipalities statewide. Additionally, the race and its run-up — pre-running begins Oct. 24 — bring excitement as high season ramps up in Los Cabos during what has been a disappointing year for tourism. International arrivals, for example, have thus far been down 8.4% in 2026, and tourism as a whole down 5.6%.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by SCORE International (@scoreinternational)

There’s a lot on the line for racers, too. San Diego’s Luke “The Luke” McMillin, for example, is attempting to complete a rare full-season sweep of the 2026 SCORE calendar, having already logged Trophy Truck class wins in the San Felipe 250, Baja 500 and Baja 400. Tyler Lynn, Carter Klein and their SLR (Slam Life Racing) Honda team, meanwhile, are attempting to go that feat one step better, aiming at a second consecutive Motorcycle class season sweep.

Chris Sands is a writer and editor for Mexico News Daily, and the former Cabo San Lucas local expert for the USA Today travel website 10 Best and writer of Fodor’s Los Cabos travel guidebook. He has also contributed to numerous other websites and publications, including The San Diego Union-Tribune, Marriott Bonvoy Traveler, Forbes Travel Guide, Porthole Cruise and Travel, and Cabo Living.

World.title: Baja California overtakes Guanajuato as Mexico’s most violent state: Tuesday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

📉 Homicides fall 30.6% year over year in September : National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 42.2 homicides per day last month, down from 60.8 per day in September 2025.

: National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported an average of 42.2 homicides per day last month, down from 60.8 per day in September 2025. 📊 Homicides down 51.4% from September 2024 : Figueroa said the decline was “more than 52%” compared to López Obrador’s final month in office, but her data showed a 51.4% reduction.

: Figueroa said the decline was “more than 52%” compared to López Obrador’s final month in office, but her data showed a 51.4% reduction. 📍 Baja California overtakes Guanajuato as Mexico’s most violent state : Baja California recorded 1,092 homicides from January to September (8.5% of the national total of 12,854), narrowly ahead of Guanajuato with 1,089.

: Baja California recorded 1,092 homicides from January to September (8.5% of the national total of 12,854), narrowly ahead of Guanajuato with 1,089. ✅ Homicides decline in all 32 states in first nine months of 2026 : San Luis Potosí recorded the steepest year-over-year drop (78.6%). Nayarit, Quintana Roo, Baja California Sur, Nuevo León and Zacatecas also saw declines of more than 50%.

: San Luis Potosí recorded the steepest year-over-year drop (78.6%). Nayarit, Quintana Roo, Baja California Sur, Nuevo León and Zacatecas also saw declines of more than 50%. 🔫 Over 14,000 weapons handed in since Sheinbaum took office : Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez said 14,077 firearms and explosive devices were “voluntarily” turned in under the Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz program between Oct. 1, 2024 and Oct. 12, 2026.

: Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez said 14,077 firearms and explosive devices were “voluntarily” turned in under the Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz program between Oct. 1, 2024 and Oct. 12, 2026. 🚨 70,571 arrests for high-impact crimes in two years : Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said authorities also seized 36,303 firearms and almost 570 tonnes of drugs, and dismantled 2,792 clandestine drug labs, between Oct. 1, 2024 and Sept. 30, 2026.

: Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said authorities also seized 36,303 firearms and almost 570 tonnes of drugs, and dismantled 2,792 clandestine drug labs, between Oct. 1, 2024 and Sept. 30, 2026. 🏥 Sheinbaum rejects claims of “crisis” in public healthcare as IMSS workers protest: Asked about the protests scheduled for Tuesday, the president acknowledged the need to hire more specialists, promised higher resident doctor scholarships in 2027 and admitted medicine distribution problems remain. She said healthcare workers’ legitimate demands would be addressed and urged them to protest peacefully.

Why today’s mañanera matters

Federal officials presented the government’s monthly security report at President Sheinbaum’s Tuesday morning press conference.

Data showed that homicides declined significantly in September, continuing a downward trend seen throughout 2026.

Sheinbaum and other officials assert that the reduction in homicides and other crimes is evidence that the government’s security strategy is working. However, there is skepticism about the accuracy of the government’s homicide numbers, which are based on data provided by Attorney General’s Offices in each of Mexico’s 32 federal entities.

While security was the main focus of today’s mañanera, Sheinbaum also fielded a question about the national protests scheduled for Tuesday, at which Mexican Social Security Institute (IMSS) healthcare workers will demand higher pay and better working conditions, and denounce a lack of medications and medical supplies at IMSS hospitals. In Mexico City, a large protest march (megamarcha) is scheduled to set off from the Siglo XXI National Medical Center on Tuesday afternoon.

Homicides fall 30% year over year in September

National Public Security System chief Marcela Figueroa reported that there was an average of 42.2 homicides per day in September, a decline of 30.6% compared to the same month of 2026.

Compared to August, the daily homicide rate rose 3.2%.

Homicides declined 51% in September compared to 2 years earlier

Figueroa said that homicides declined “more than 52%” last month compared to September 2024, the final month of Andrés Manuel López Obrador’s presidency.

However, the data she presented showed a slightly lower reduction of 51.4%. There was an average of 86.9 homicides per day in September 2024, compared to an average of 42.2 per day last month.

Figueroa presented data that showed that last month was the least violent September of any year since 2015.

Baja California overtakes Guanajuato as Mexico’s most violent state

Figueroa reported that Baja California recorded the highest number of homicides among Mexico’s 32 federal entities in the first nine months of 2026. There were 1,092 homicides in the northern border state between January and September, representing 8.5% of the national total (12,854).

The murder count in Baja California was slightly higher than that in Guanajuato, which has been Mexico’s most violent state in terms of homicides in recent years. Until the end of August, Guanajuato was the most violent state in 2026 as well.

However, in the nine months to the end of September, Guanajuato ranked as the second most violent state, recording 1,089 homicides or 8.5% of the national total.

The five states that recorded the next highest homicide counts in the first nine months of 2026 were:

Chihuahua: 1,009 (7.8% of the national total)

Sinaloa: 987 (7.7%)

México state: 818 (6.4%)

Guerrero: 731 (5.7%)

Morelos: 673 (5.2%)

The seven states with the highest murder counts between January and September accounted for almost half (49.8%) of all homicides perpetrated in Mexico in the period.

Oaxaca, Jalisco and Michoacán ranked eighth, ninth and tenth, respectively, for total homicides in the first nine months of 2026. Mexico City ranked 12th with 585 homicides.

Yucatán recorded the lowest number of homicides among Mexico’s 32 federal entities, with just 21 between January and September.

Homicides declined in every state in the first 9 months of 2026

Figueroa reported that homicides declined in every federal entity in the first nine months of the year. Compared to the January-September period of last year, homicides fell 78.6% in San Luis Potosí, the largest reduction of any state.

Five other states recorded year-over-year declines in homicides of more than 50%. They were:

Nayarit: 69.5%

Quintana Roo: 59.7%

Baja California Sur: 54.6%

Nuevo León: 51.5%

Zacatecas: 50.4%

Mexicans have handed in more than 14,000 firearms and explosive devices since Sheinbaum took office

Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez reported that 14,077 firearms and explosive devices were “voluntarily” handed over to authorities between Oct. 1, 2024 — the date Sheinbaum was sworn in as president — and Oct. 12, 2026. The weapons were turned in under the government program Sí al Desarme, Sí a la Paz (Yes to Disarmament, Yes to Peace).

Rodríguez noted that people who handed over weapons received cash from authorities. She also said that children have exchanged more than 15,000 “war toys” for “educational toys” since Sheinbaum took office.

Over 70,000 arrests since Sheinbaum took office

Security Minister Omar García Harfuch reported that 70,571 people were arrested for allegedly committing high-impact crimes between Oct. 1, 2024 and Sept. 30, 2026. Among the offenses classified as high-impact crimes are murder, kidnapping, violent robbery, rape and extortion.

According to the information presented by García Harfuch, authorities seized 36,303 firearms and almost 570 tonnes of drugs between Oct. 1, 2024, and Sept. 30, 2026.

In addition, authorities dismantled 2,792 clandestine drug laboratories in the same period.

Sheinbaum pledges to address the concerns of protesting healthcare workers

A reporter asked the president what message she would send to IMSS workers planning to protest on Thursday.

Sheinbaum first pointed to her government’s healthcare achievements.

“It’s important that what we’ve done in two years is known,” she said before reporting a range of achievements, including the construction of 34 new public hospitals and the opening or modernization of 650 operating rooms.

“We haven’t had our arms crossed. We’ve been working intensely for two years to support the country’s healthcare system,” Sheinbaum said.

She acknowledged that there is more to do, specifically noting that authorities need to hire more specialist doctors for the public health system. Sheinbaum also said that resident doctors’ “scholarships” need to be increased, and pledged that would happen in 2027.

“They earn less than the minimum wage,” she said.

“And a lot of the time the work of specialists falls on them. … The operation of [public] hospitals is supported by them in many cases,” Sheinbaum said.

She also said that the government has work to do to resolve problems related to the distribution of medications, although she indicated that the Rutas de la Salud (Health Routes) program — which delivers medicines and medical supplies to public healthcare facilities — is functioning well.

Sheinbaum said her government would address legitimate demands of public healthcare workers, but rejected claims that there is a “crisis” in Mexico’s health system. She said that healthcare workers have the “freedom” to protest, but urged them to do so peacefully.

“The objective is to have the best healthcare system and make progress on [addressing] some deficiencies we’ve had for some time,” Sheinbaum said.

World.title: Army rescues 32 in Ensenada as floods and landslides endanger lives on Mexico’s Pacific coast
World.content:
Air search and rescue operations are ramping up as twin storm systems batter Mexico’s Pacific coast, causing the deaths of at least five people.

In response to Hurricanes Rachel and Simon, the Defense Ministry (Sedena) has activated Plan DN-III-E, its operational emergency management plan that places thousands of soldiers, sailors and national guardsmen on alert to protect and aid civilians during natural disasters. Some 14,000 federal and state agents were deployed across Baja California to respond to the emergency.

Soldiers and guardsmen on Monday rescued 32 people stranded outside Ensenada, Baja California, after a mudslide caused by Tropical Storm Rachel cut off their only escape route.

The Air Force employed a “UH-60” Black Hawk helicopter to carry out three air operations, rescuing 22 foreign nationals, 10 Mexicans and three dogs.

The evacuees were members of the Genesis religious community, a Christian ministry that operates orphan care, camps and community outreach programs just outside the port city in the northwestern part of the peninsula.

Rachel, now wreaking havoc in southern California and places as far inland as Las Vegas, has already claimed the lives of four people — including two children — in Mexico.

Ejército Mexicano, Fuerza Aérea y Guardia Nacional rescata a 32 personas y tres caninos en Ensenada, Baja California. Este 12 de octubre del presente año, personal del Ejército, Fuerza Aérea y Guardia Nacional como parte de la aplicación del Plan DN-III-E realizaron una operación aérea de búsqueda y rescate, con el fin de evacuar a integrantes de una congregación religiosa que quedaron aislados en el rancho “Genesis”, Ensenada, B.C., debido a un deslizamiento de tierra que dificultó el acceso terrestre a la zona el cual fue provocado por las fuertes lluvias de la tormenta tropical “Rachel”. Ante las condiciones adversas del terreno, clima y las dificultades para acceder por vía terrestre, la Fuerza Aérea Mexicana empleó un helicóptero UH-60, cuya tripulación ejecutó tres operaciones aéreas que permitieron rescatar exitosamente a 22 personas extranjeras, 10 de nacionalidad mexicana y 3 caninos que se encontraban imposibilitados para trasladarse a un lugar seguro, a quienes se les proporcionó atención médica oportuna. Con estas acciones, el Ejército Mexicano, la Fuerza Aérea y la Guardia Nacional, refrendan su compromiso de brindar el auxilio necesario en situaciones de emergencia, poniendo todas sus capacidades operativas, preparación y recursos al servicio de la población, con el objetivo prioritario de salvaguardar la vida y la integridad de las personas. #EjércitoMexicano #FuerzaAéreaMx #GuardiaNacional — @Defensamx (@Defensamx1) October 13, 2026

Baja authorities say at least five others remain missing as floodwaters swept away vehicles, damaged homes and knocked out electricity in Ensenada, while landslides and overflowing rivers were causing problems across the state.

In addition to Sedena’s efforts, Tijuana’s mayor ordered specialized personnel from the municipality’s Security Ministry to support operations in Ensenada, about 80 kilometers (50 miles) to the south.

The Tijuana delegation includes specialists from the Fire Department trained in rescue maneuvers in rugged terrain and hydrometeorological contingency situations, members of the Canine Unit and agents from its Search Cell division.

Farther south, Hurricane Simon is following in Rachel’s path.

Simon claimed the life of a 71-year-old man in Chilpancingo, Guerrero, while also downing trees and electricity poles, making roads impassable and flooding homes in coastal towns.

Though Simon has weakened to a Category 1 hurricane, it is expected to maintain hurricane strength through Wednesday, though its short-term direction and intensity track has defied forecasters’ expectations.

About 127 to 255 millimeters (5 to 10 inches) of rain are expected from Simon across coastal west-central Mexico, with as much as 380 mm (15 inches) in the state of Sinaloa by Thursday.

Flooding and landslides have also been reported in the states of Michoacán and Colima.

With reports from Reporte Índigo, The Guardian, CBS News and La Jornada

World.title: Flávio Skips Band Debate as Lula Confirms
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

Politics: Brazil

Runoff · Sunday, 25 October Flávio Bolsonaro vs Lula: what happens next First-round results, how the runoff works, the key dates and who backs whom, in one guide. Read the runoff guide →

Key Facts —



Who. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula, the two candidates in Brazil’s presidential runoff on Sunday 25 October 2026. —



What. Flávio said on Tuesday 13 October that he does not plan to attend Band’s runoff debate on Sunday 18 October. Lula confirmed that he will go. —



Why. Neither candidate joined a joint debate in round one, so the runoff could again pass without a face-to-face meeting. —



Still open. Flávio’s team will decide on Globo’s debate on Friday 23 October. The media pool debate on Thursday 15 October still needs both candidates to confirm. —



Prediction markets. Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 86% and Kalshi at 88% (Lula: 15% and 14%), as of 14 October, 1:20 am ET; prices are bets, not polls.

Flávio Bolsonaro said on Tuesday that he does not plan to go to Band’s runoff debate on Sunday, while Lula confirmed. Here are the dates, the US times and what is still open before the 25 October vote.

What Flávio Said on 13 October

Flávio, the conservative senator who led round one, told reporters on Tuesday 13 October that he is not going to the Band debate, adding that attendance is “not planned”. Poder360 reported the remark after 17 regional branches of the MDB party announced support for his candidacy.

On the Globo debate of 23 October, Flávio said his campaign team would have the final word, Poder360 reported. Lula, by contrast, confirmed that he will attend and said he hopes his opponent will show up, CNN Brasil reported.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Debate Calendar at a Glance

Brazil votes in the runoff on Sunday 25 October. Four television debates were announced for the final two weeks, and one has already been cancelled.

Event Date Broadcaster Status Record debate Sunday 11 October Record Cancelled by the broadcaster Media pool debate, “O Momento da Decisão” Thursday 15 October 11 outlets, including SBT, CNN Brasil and RedeTV! Needs both candidates to confirm; start time not announced Band and Estadão debate Sunday 18 October, 8 p.m. Brasília (7 p.m. US Eastern) Band, with Estadão and partner outlets Lula confirmed; Flávio says he is not going Globo debate Friday 23 October, after the Jornal Nacional news TV Globo, GloboNews and g1 Flávio’s team to decide Globo interviews Lula on Thursday 15 October, Flávio on Friday 16 October TV Globo, after the Jornal Nacional news Scheduled

A UE2020 electronic voting machine of the kind used in Brazilian elections. (File photo)

Band on 18 October

Band and Estadão announced their debate for Sunday 18 October at 8 p.m. Brasília time. That is 7 p.m. on the US East Coast and 4 p.m. on the West Coast.

Partner outlets include TV Cultura, TV Gazeta and Jovem Pan, and the debate is also due to stream on Estadão and YouTube. Band had first planned it for 11 October before moving it a week later.

Globo on 23 October

Globo has set its debate for Friday 23 October, after the evening news, two days before the vote. César Tralli is due to moderate, and the programme is planned for TV Globo, GloboNews and the g1 news site.

Globo will also interview each candidate alone. Lula is due on Thursday 15 October, interviewed by Renata Lo Prete, and Flávio on Friday 16 October.

The Pool Debate on 15 October and the Cancelled Record Debate

A pool of 11 outlets plans a debate called “O Momento da Decisão” (The Moment of Decision) on Thursday 15 October. Its members include CNN Brasil, Exame, Metrópoles, Nova Brasil FM, Rádio Itatiaia, RedeTV!, Rede Vida, SBT, SBT News, Terra and Veja+ TV.

Whether it happens depends on both candidates confirming, O Povo reported on 13 October. Lula’s Globo interview falls on the same day.

The Record debate planned for Sunday 11 October was cancelled by the broadcaster, which cited incompatible schedules. No new date for Record has been announced.

Why Round One Had No Joint Debate

Lula and Flávio did not take part in joint debates before the first round. On 1 October, Flávio pulled out of the Globo debate shortly before it started, citing what he called censorship by the electoral court TSE over the show’s rules.

Lula had also said he would not attend, and Globo then cancelled the debate. For the runoff, both men said they would take part, Lula on 5 October and Flávio on 6 October.

What Prediction Markets Say

Traders on Polymarket and Kalshi price Flávio Bolsonaro as the favourite for 25 October, and the box below shows the latest prices. Kalshi is regulated in the US by the CFTC, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 86.1% · Lula 14.5% (US$181 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 88% · Lula 14% As of 14 October, 1:20 am ET (06:20 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

The latest Datafolha poll we have verified, from 8 October, had Flávio on 49% and Lula on 45% of all voters. Among valid votes, the poll gave Flávio 52% and Lula 48%.

What It Means for You

If you follow Brazil from the United States, a debate without the poll leader gives you fewer live moments to judge the candidates. Watch the Globo decision, because that is the last debate before the vote.

Investors in Brazilian shares and the real tend to watch prediction markets and polls around such events. A debate that shifts those numbers can move local assets the next morning, so the Monday session in São Paulo is worth watching.

Our election hub keeps the full runoff calendar. We will update this page when a broadcaster confirms or drops a date.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether Flávio will attend the Globo debate, or whether Lula and Flávio will both appear on 15 October. The sources we checked give no start time for the pool debate.

It is also not known whether Band will go ahead with one candidate or change the format. Rules and the number of questions have not been published in the sources we checked.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will Flávio Bolsonaro attend the Band debate?

Flávio said on Tuesday 13 October that he does not plan to go to the Band debate on Sunday 18 October. Lula confirmed that he will attend.

When are the Brazil runoff debates?

Band and Estadão plan a debate on Sunday 18 October and Globo one on Friday 23 October. A media pool debate on Thursday 15 October still needs both candidates to confirm.

What time is the Band debate in the United States?

It starts at 8 p.m. in Brasília on Sunday 18 October. That is 7 p.m. US Eastern and 4 p.m. US Pacific.

Will Flávio Bolsonaro go to the Globo debate?

That is open. He said his campaign team will have the final word on the debate planned for Friday 23 October.

Why did the Record debate on 11 October not happen?

Record cancelled it, citing incompatible schedules, according to O Povo. No new date has been announced.

When is the Brazil runoff?

The runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro is on Sunday 25 October 2026. It follows the first round on Sunday 4 October.

World.title: Argentina’s 1.9% Inflation and Your Budget
World.content:
Save Share In short Contents Listen Aa

The Palacio de Hacienda in Buenos Aires, home of the Economy Ministry, whose Treasury keeps a dollar account at the central bank. File photo. (Photo: Elsapucai, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

ARGENTINA · EXPATS & NOMADS

Key Facts — The country Argentina, whose peso prices rise month after month, so every expat budget there needs a yearly inflation check.

— The numbers Consumer prices rose 1.9% in September 2026 and 33.4% over 12 months, according to INDEC, the statistics institute.

— The pressure points Housing, water, electricity and gas rose 3.1% in the month, and education 3.0%; restaurants and hotels rose 1.1%.

— Why now INDEC published the September figure on Tuesday 13 October, after 1.7% in August.

— What it means for you Utilities and school fees rose fastest; at the official sell rate of 1,535 pesos per dollar, one million pesos is about US$651.

— Prediction markets Polymarket prices Argentina’s annual inflation for 2026 at 30.0% to 34.9% with 64.9% probability (US$79,918 traded; 14 October, 00:52 ET).

— Still open Whether October stays near 1.7%, as the central bank’s analyst survey expects, and how rents move.

Argentina’s consumer prices rose 1.9% in September 2026, up from 1.7% in August, INDEC reported on Tuesday 13 October. Over 12 months, prices are 33.4% higher.

For foreigners who pay their costs in pesos, a rise of that size changes a household budget within a season. Here is where the increases landed and what to watch next.

What INDEC Reported

INDEC’s figure matched the 1.9% that the central bank’s analyst survey (REM, Relevamiento de Expectativas de Mercado) had expected, according to Infobae. August’s 1.7% was the lowest monthly rate in 14 months, so September is a step up, not a surprise.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Argentina ranks 4th of 14 with 61.2 points. Strongest pillar: future resources (68); weakest: economic relationships (23). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (B-); inflation of 42%; public debt at 80% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The accumulated rise from January to September is 23.6%. If the 1.9% pace repeated for twelve months, prices would rise about 25%, which shows why the monthly number matters for planning.

File photo: the Banco Central de la República Argentina in Buenos Aires, whose analyst survey (REM) tracks inflation expectations.

This guide condensed into 3 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Free. The same address also receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing with an expat desk. We send a confirmation link first and nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves. Privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

Where Prices Rose Most

Housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels led with 3.1%, according to INDEC via Perfil. Education rose 3.0%.

Category September rise Housing, water, electricity, gas 3.1% Education 3.0% Seasonal items (vegetables, legumes) 2.9% Regulated prices (gas, electricity, health plans) 2.3% Core inflation (excludes seasonal and regulated) 1.7% Clothing and footwear 1.4% Restaurants and hotels 1.1%

Seasonal items rose 2.9% and regulated prices 2.3%, while core inflation, which strips both out, was 1.7%. Analysts quoted by Infobae said the acceleration came mainly from volatile items and tariffs, not from underlying price trends.

Regions differ. Greater Buenos Aires and the Pampas region rose 2.0% and Patagonia 1.4%, the lowest, according to Infobae.

What It Means for Your Budget

Utility bills and school fees rose fastest, and those are the costs that foreign families feel first. Restaurants and hotels rose 1.1%, the smallest rise in the table, which is easier on visitors than on residents paying bills.

At the official Banco Nación sell rate of 1,535 pesos per dollar, ARS 1,000,000 is about US$651. The blue (informal) rate sold at 1,550 on Tuesday evening, about 1.0% above the official rate, and the CCL (contado con liquidación, a rate for dollars bought through securities) sold at 1,613.8, about 5.1% above, according to DolarApi.

Our news report on the figure has the market reaction. Check the rate your landlord or bank actually uses before you convert a peso price.

What Markets and Analysts Expect

The REM survey expects about 1.7% for October, according to Infobae. That is a forecast by named analysts, not a result.

On Polymarket, a prediction market where users bet real money, traders price Argentina’s annual inflation for 2026 at 30.0% to 34.9% with a probability of 64.9%, and 25.0% to 29.9% at 30.0% (US$79,918 traded; 14 October, 00:52 ET). These are bets, not forecasts by officials.

What Prediction Markets Say

Argentina’s 2026 inflation. Polymarket prices the year’s annual inflation at 30.0% to 34.9% at 64.9% and 25.0% to 29.9% at 30.0% (US$79,918 traded). Stand: 14 October, 00:52 ET. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

We do not know October’s figure, which INDEC publishes in November. We also cannot say how rents moved, because the sources we read give only category averages.

Inflation in Argentina has eased from far higher levels and moves in waves. The next few releases will show whether September was a bump or a turn.

More: Argentina news in English, every day from The Rio Times. Also in today’s LatAm Expat & Nomad Daily Guide.

Frequently Asked Questions

What was Argentina’s inflation in September 2026?

INDEC reported on Tuesday 13 October 2026 that consumer prices rose 1.9% in September, after 1.7% in August. Prices were 33.4% higher than a year earlier and 23.6% higher than in December 2025.

Which prices rose most in September?

Housing, water, electricity and gas rose 3.1%, and education 3.0%. Restaurants and hotels rose 1.1%, the smallest increase among the categories listed here.

What do analysts expect for October?

The central bank’s survey of analysts, the REM, expects about 1.7% for October, according to Infobae. That is a forecast, and INDEC publishes the October figure in November.

The Short Version In short: Your LatAm expat and nomad daily guide for Wednesday, 14 October 2026. Panama begins reopening its public schools today, five days after the magnitude 7.7 earthquake. Hurricane Simon is now a Category 1 storm and is forecast to reach the coast near Mazatlán, Mexico, on Thursday 15 October. Argentina’s inflation rose to 1.9% in September, and US inflation data arrives at 8:30 a.m. New York time. Prediction markets price a Flávio Bolsonaro win of Brazil’s presidency near 86% (bets, not polls). 01 Panama: schools reopen in stages. The education ministry counts 619 damaged schools, 35 of them destroyed. Our The education ministry counts 619 damaged schools, 35 of them destroyed. Our report on the state of emergency sets out what changes. 02 Mexico: Simon weakens but lingers. Mexico’s weather service has a hurricane watch for the Sinaloa coast from Escuinapa to Bahía Tempehuaya. Our Mexico’s weather service has a hurricane watch for the Sinaloa coast from Escuinapa to Bahía Tempehuaya. Our checklist for foreigners says what to prepare. 03 Argentina: prices rose 1.9% in a month. Over 12 months, consumer prices are up 33.4%. Our Over 12 months, consumer prices are up 33.4%. Our guide to what this means for expats has the detail. What changed since yesterday INDEC, Argentina’s statistics institute, published September inflation on Tuesday: 1.9% for the month, against 1.7% in August. Hurricane Simon fell from Category 2 to Category 1, and Panama’s ministry announced a gradual reopening of public schools from Wednesday. Mexico’s peso weakened about 0.6% on Tuesday, to 18.37 per US dollar.

00 The LatAm Expat Nomad Daily Guide Status Board

Story Yesterday Now Direction Hurricane Simon Category 2 (Mon afternoon) Category 1 (Tue) Weaker, still heading for Sinaloa Panama public schools Closed Tuesday Gradual reopening from Wednesday Slow return Argentina inflation (monthly) August: 1.7% September: 1.9% Faster in the month Brazil PTAX (sell) Fri 9 Oct: 4.9892 Tue 13 Oct: 5.0096 Real weaker (no fixing Monday) Mexico peso (RT close) Mon 12 Oct: 18.263 Tue 13 Oct: 18.371 Peso softer Colombia TRM 3,194.44 (10–13 Oct) 3,181.74 (Wed 14 Oct) Peso firmer

01 Getting Around

Panama: schools and daily routines. Panama’s education ministry (Meduca) said on Tuesday 13 October that the gradual reopening of public schools begins on Wednesday 14 October, once safety inspections are done. Minister Ventura Vega counted 619 damaged schools in 15 education regions, and 35 schools destroyed, according to Infobae and Telemetro.

Not every building will open on the same day. Ask your child’s school which building is open and when, because the reopening depends on each inspection.

File photo: the seafront in Mazatlán, Sinaloa, where Hurricane Simon is forecast to reach the coast.

RT Ask Rio Times Straight answers about living in Latin America, from our reporting. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas in Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times Straight answers about living in Latin America, from our reporting. × Cost of living Is it safe? Visas Neighborhoods Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

Mexico’s Pacific coast: Hurricane Simon. Mexico’s weather service (SMN) reported on Tuesday that Simon was a Category 1 hurricane, with sustained winds of 150 km/h (93 mph) and gusts to 185 km/h. It was about 155 km (96 miles) west of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, and 320 km (200 miles) south of Mazatlán, according to La Razón and El Financiero.

The weather service expects Simon to reach the coast near Mazatlán as a Category 1 hurricane on Thursday 15 October, according to El Mañana. Forecast rain is 50 to 75 millimetres on Nayarit’s coast and in southern Sinaloa, with waves of 2 to 3 metres.

A hurricane watch (hurricane conditions are possible) covers the coast from Escuinapa to Bahía Tempehuaya, and a prevention zone for hurricane-force winds covers the Marías Islands. Alerts change with each bulletin, and we could not read the latest US National Hurricane Center advisory this morning. Our checklist for foreigners sets out what to prepare.

The LatAm Brief One email, every weekday morning. What moved in Latin American markets, politics and expat life. Yesterday’s subject line: “IMF cuts Brazil growth to 2.2% and Argentina's to 2.1%” Get the brief Free. We send a confirmation link first — nothing arrives until you click it. Unsubscribe with one click in any edition. If you stop opening us for 30 days we stop sending by ourselves, as we assume the interest is no longer there. See our privacy policy. We never share your email.

Colombia: marches today. Unions and teachers march on Wednesday 14 October, and Bogotá’s city government lists protest events with a union march from Parque Nacional at 9:30 a.m. Bogotá time. Expect slower traffic and changes to TransMilenio (the city’s bus system) around Carrera Séptima, Carrera Décima and Calle 26; our report on the marches has the places and times.

Brazil: loud weeks, normal days. Campaigning continues until the runoff on Sunday 25 October, 11 days away. Most foreign residents cannot vote.

02 Cost of Living & Money

Each measure is labelled, and dates differ by country. Brazil’s PTAX, Colombia’s TRM and Argentina’s rates are official or public-service quotes; Mexico, Peru and Chile are Tuesday market closes from RT, a market-data provider, not official fixings.

Brazil. The PTAX fixing (the central bank’s reference dollar rate) was 5.0096 reais to sell on Tuesday 13 October, after 4.9892 on Friday 9 October. Monday was a holiday with no fixing. At 5.0096, R$1,000 is about US$200.

Mexico. The dollar closed at 18.371 pesos on Tuesday 13 October, up from 18.263 on Monday 12 October. It is not the official FIX rate (Banxico’s daily reference rate). At 18.371, MXN 10,000 is about US$544.

Chile. The market close was 982.5 pesos per dollar on Tuesday 13 October, a market-data quote, because we could not read the central bank’s observado (its reference rate) this morning. At 982.5, CLP 1,000,000 is about US$1,018.

Colombia. The TRM (the official representative rate) is 3,181.74 pesos per dollar for Wednesday 14 October, down from 3,194.44 for 10 to 13 October, according to the financial regulator’s open data. At 3,181.74, COP 1,000,000 is about US$314.

Argentina. DolarApi shows the official Banco Nación rate at 1,485 to buy and 1,535 to sell. The blue (informal market rate) was 1,530 and 1,550 on Tuesday evening, and the CCL (contado con liquidación, a rate for dollars bought through securities) was 1,611.1 and 1,613.8. ARS 1,000,000 is about US$651 at the official sell rate and about US$620 at the CCL sell rate, and ArgentinaDatos puts country risk (the extra yield investors demand on Argentine dollar bonds) at 597 points on 13 October.

Peru. We could not obtain SUNAT’s (the tax authority’s) rate. The market close was 3.4306 soles per dollar on Tuesday 13 October, and banks quote their own rates. At 3.4306, PEN 1,000 is about US$291.

The wider picture. The real is about 0.4% weaker since Friday, Mexico’s peso weakened about 0.6% on Tuesday, and Colombia’s peso is about 0.4% stronger on the TRM. One day does not set a trend, and currencies often overshoot after news and then settle.

03 Visas, Residency & Tax

Argentina: what 33.4% inflation means for your budget. Argentina’s statistics institute INDEC reported consumer prices up 1.9% in September and 33.4% over 12 months. Housing, water, electricity and gas rose 3.1% in the month, which matters most for anyone renting or paying utility bills.

Colombia: 17 days left. Foreigners holding a permanent-resident visa issued under earlier rules must transfer it before 31 October 2026, the Foreign Ministry has reiterated. The process is online; the ministry advises using its official site without intermediaries. Our earlier explainer sets out who is affected.

Peru: regional runoff on 6 December. The electoral court (JNE) moved the second round of the regional elections from Sunday 29 November to Sunday 6 December, according to Gestión. Foreign residents cannot vote for governors, and our expat guide to the runoffs carries the new date.

Panama: the US$300,000 investor visa. Our explainer on the 15 October date, which falls tomorrow, sets out the real-estate threshold and what the 2024 decree said. Check the current rules with Panama’s immigration service or a licensed lawyer before you commit money.

Brazil: foreigners and the runoff. Most foreign residents cannot vote. A Datafolha poll released on 8 October (2,520 interviews, 6 to 8 October, margin of error 2 points) put Flávio Bolsonaro at 49% and Lula at 45% in the runoff, a gap at the edge of the poll’s margin of error, and polls are snapshots. Our runoff guide covers the practical side.

04 What Prediction Markets Say

Brazil’s presidency. Polymarket prices Flávio Bolsonaro at 86.1% and Lula at 13.5% to win (US$181.2 million traded). Stand: 14 October, 00:52 ET. Argentina’s 2026 inflation. Polymarket prices the year’s annual inflation at 30.0% to 34.9% at 64.9% and 25.0% to 29.9% at 30.0% (US$79,918 traded). Stand: 14 October, 00:52 ET. Mexico’s central bank in November. Polymarket prices no change at 75.5% and a 0.25-point cut at 21.2% (US$53,907 traded). Stand: 14 October, 00:52 ET. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

05 The Calendar Ahead

Wed 14 Oct US consumer inflation for September at 8:30 a.m. New York time, 1:30 p.m. Lisbon time (the RT calendar forecast is 3.6% over 12 months, against 3.4% before), a data point for the dollar against every currency above.

Wed 14 Oct Union and teacher marches in Bogotá and other Colombian cities.

Thu 15 Oct Hurricane Simon may reach the coast near Mazatlán, according to Mexico’s weather service. Forecasts may change.

Thu 15 Oct September inflation in the Dominican Republic and Ecuador, and Peru’s September unemployment rate (the RT calendar forecast is 5.0%, against 4.8% before).

Thu 22 Oct Mexico’s mid-October inflation (the RT calendar forecast is 0.3% for the fortnight).

Fri 23 Oct Brazil’s October mid-month inflation (IPCA-15), with a forecast of 4.6% over 12 months against 4.47% before, from the RT calendar.

Sun 25 Oct Brazil’s presidential runoff, with voting from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Brasília time.

Tue 27 Oct Chile’s central bank decides its interest rate (4.5% before), according to the RT calendar.

Sat 31 Oct Colombia’s deadline to transfer older permanent-resident visas.

Tue 3 – Wed 4 Nov Brazil’s central bank sets its Selic rate (Brazil’s benchmark interest rate, now 13.75%).

Dates come from official calendars and the RT economic calendar; forecasts are not ours. The region does not move as one block, and each release can push a currency either way.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where is Hurricane Simon expected to make landfall? Mexico’s weather service expects Simon, a Category 1 hurricane on Tuesday 13 October 2026, to reach the coast near Mazatlán, Sinaloa, on Thursday 15 October. A hurricane watch covers the Sinaloa coast from Escuinapa to Bahía Tempehuaya. Forecast points can shift, so check the latest official bulletin. When do Panama’s schools reopen after the earthquake? Panama’s education ministry said public schools begin a gradual reopening on Wednesday 14 October 2026, after safety inspections. It counts 619 damaged schools, 35 of them destroyed, after the magnitude 7.7 quake of Friday 9 October. Which buildings open first is not yet known. What was Argentina’s inflation in September 2026? INDEC, Argentina’s statistics institute, reported on Tuesday 13 October 2026 that consumer prices rose 1.9% in September, after 1.7% in August. Prices were 33.4% higher than a year earlier, and 23.6% higher than in December 2025.

A warm, showery Wednesday suits a museum morning and a lively indoor evening.

The day’s cultural pick is MASP on Avenida Paulista, open 10am to 6pm with tickets until 5pm.

The business mood is cautious, with Latin American stocks and currencies softening as investors watch Brazil’s runoff.

In one line: see great art, eat well in Centro, and plan around scattered rain.

São Paulo Daily Brief for Wednesday, October 14, 2026. Photo: The Rio Times archive.

01

Weather & What to Wear

FOUR-DAY OUTLOOK

WED 14 24°C 80% rain THU 15 23°C 75% rain FRI 16 22°C 70% rain SAT 17 21°C 60% rain

Today feels warm and humid, with frequent showers likely from mid-morning. The rain will be heavy at times, so keep a small umbrella on hand.

Wear light, breathable layers and comfortable shoes that can handle wet pavements. A waterproof jacket works better than a flimsy poncho.

The rest of the week stays warm, humid and unsettled. Thursday and Friday bring more of the same, with a slightly cooler and drier Saturday.

Day at a Glance

SNAPSHOT

— Weather: Warm and humid, showery from late morning — The day’s event: MASP open 10am–6pm, tickets R$85 until 5pm — Venue/time: Avenida Paulista, 1578 — Bela Vista — Markets: Ibovespa fell 1.04% to 206,888 and the real weakened 0.81% to 5.0273 per dollar on Tuesday — Weekend/outlook: Rain eases slightly Saturday, more of the same Sunday — The day for: Art, coffee and a long lunch indoors A day made for slow looking and good food, not for rushing.

03

What to See & Do

WEDNESDAY IN SÃO PAULO

TODAY’S PICK — ART & RAIN MASP on Avenida Paulista MASP is the right call for a showery Wednesday. It is open 10am to 6pm, with ticket entry until 5pm. Tickets cost R$85 and Wednesdays are full-price days. You can also walk the Paulista stretch afterwards. The museum sits at Avenida Paulista, 1578, in Bela Vista. The nearest Metrô station is Trianon-MASP on Line 2 Green. Take your time with the glass easels and the collection. The building itself is a work of art. Afterwards, a short walk takes you to Praça do Ciclista or a shopping centre café if rain is falling.

OUTDOORS — BETWEEN SHOWERS Parque Ibirapuera for fresh air Ibirapuera Park is free to enter. Today’s rain means carrying a brolly and keeping to the hard paths. Head to the park in Vila Mariana between downpours. It is a good space for a quick walk or jog before rain returns. Do not plan a long picnic. Think of this as a break between indoor plans.

COFFEE & WHERE TO WORK — PINHEIROS & JARDINS Laptop-friendly spots with wifi Coffee shops in Pinheiros suit a working morning. Many offer wifi, plugs and a calm room to sit with a laptop. Try a stretch of Rua dos Pinheiros, where several cafés serve good espresso and light food. In Jardins, the area around Rua Oscar Freire has air-conditioned options for a longer session. Arrive early to grab a window seat.

THE CONTRASTING PLAY — DOWNTOWN CALM Centro and a quieter pace Skip the mall crowds and walk through Centro’s older streets when the rain eases. The architecture rewards slow looking. Mercado Municipal is free to enter. It is loud and steamy — a full contrast to a quiet gallery. Combine it with a simple lunch in Liberdade, a short Metrô ride away on Line 1 Blue.

TONIGHT, AFTER 7 PM A slow dinner and a drink For tonight, choose a restaurant in Pinheiros or Itaim Bibi where you can linger over dinner without rushing. Pinheiros has small wine bars and Japanese counters open late on weekdays. Book a table if you want a specific spot. Itaim Bibi is dressier and pricier, but it works for a proper meal after a damp day. Avoid walking far in heavy rain between venues. Pick one neighbourhood and stay there.

ALSO ON TODAY MASP — Avenida Paulista, 1578 — 10am–6pm, tickets R$85 until 5pm, major museum Sesc Pompeia — Rua Clélia, 93 — 10am–7pm, free, strong architecture and shows Japan House São Paulo — Avenida Paulista, 52 — 10am–6pm, free, design and exhibitions Pinacoteca de São Paulo — Praça da Luz, 2 — 10am–6pm, R$40, classic Brazilian art Museu do Ipiranga — Rua dos Patriotas, 300 — 10am–5pm, free on Wednesdays Museu da Língua Portuguesa — Praça da Luz — 9am–4:30pm, Tuesday to Sunday

04

Getting Around

TRANSPORT

The Metrô single fare is R$5.40. For today, check Lines 1, 2 and 3 for crowd build-up in the morning and early evening.

Today’s rodízio restrictions apply in the expanded centre, with plates ending in 5 and 6 restricted from 7am to 10am and 5pm to 8pm. Ride-hailing apps will be busy during downpours, so expect higher prices at peak rain.

05

Where to Eat

LUNCH & DINNER

Lunch: Try a simple plate at Casa do Porco in Centro or a pastel at Mercado Municipal. Both keep lunch casual and under R$80 per person.

Dinner: For dinner, look at Pinheiros for a quieter izakaya or Itaim Bibi for a proper Brazilian grill. Budget R$120–R$200 per person with a drink.

06

Practical Info

GOOD TO KNOW

Carry a small umbrella and keep a light waterproof layer in your bag. Most cafés and museums have air-conditioning, so a thin jumper helps indoors.

Pix is the easiest way to pay, but cards are widely accepted. Keep R$40–R$80 in cash for small stalls and tips.

Be careful with phones at busy Metrô turnstiles and on Avenida Paulista. Keep your device in a front pocket, especially when moving through crowds.

07

Community & Lifestyle

FOR NEWCOMERS

Expat and nomad groups often post midweek coffee meetups in Pinheiros and Vila Madalena. A quick search on community boards will show what is on for tonight.

Newcomers should start with language exchanges that meet in bars around Vila Madalena on weeknights. Arrive early and use the Metrô to avoid wet streets.

08

Game Day

MIDWEEK WATCH

Palmeiras play Fluminense tonight at the Maracanã in Rio in the first leg of their Copa Libertadores semi-final, with kick-off at 21:30 Brasília time. The return leg is at Palmeiras’ Nubank Parque on 21 October.

If you want a football atmosphere tonight, Vila Madalena bars are the place to watch the match.

For a reliable screen and good beer, try a sports bar on Rua Aspicuelta in Vila Madalena. Book if it is raining, as tables fill quickly.

Ask at the bar before settling in — not every screen shows the match you want.

09

Business & Markets

WEEK IN FIGURES

Latin American stocks and currencies broadly weakened on Tuesday as investors weighed Brazil’s presidential runoff.

Argentina’s September inflation came in at 1.9% month-on-month, a second month below 2%. The Brazilian real lost 0.81% to 5.0273 per dollar, and the Ibovespa fell 1.04%.

For expat professionals paid in dollars, a weaker real raises purchasing power, while those paid in reais face dearer imports. US inflation data today could move the currency again.

10

Plan Ahead

THE WEEK

THE DAYS AHEAD WED 14 — MASP 10am–6pm; warm with showers; rodízio plates 5 and 6 THU 15 — More rain; Sesc Pompeia free from 10am; reserve a rainy-day lunch FRI 16 — Wet again; Pinacoteca 10am–6pm; plan an indoor evening in Pinheiros SAT 17 — Cooler, rain easing; free Saturday at Pinacoteca; weekend rodízio off SUN 18 — Same damp pattern; Mercado Municipal; museums check Sunday hours

Background: São Paulo Nightlife Tonight: Robbie Williams, Blue Note Shows.

Background: São Paulo Daily Brief.

11

FAQ

QUICK ANSWERS

Is MASP free today?

No. MASP is free only on Tuesdays. Today, Wednesday 14 October 2026, the full ticket is R$85. The museum is open 10am to 6pm, with ticket entry until 5pm. It is at Avenida Paulista, 1578, near Trianon-MASP station on the green line.

Do I need cash or is Pix enough?

Pix works in most places, including museums, cafés and restaurants. Cards are also widely accepted. Keep a small amount of cash, around R$40–R$80, for street stalls or tips.

Can I walk around Ibirapuera today?

Yes, the park is free to enter. But today is showery, so you will need an umbrella and a plan to duck indoors quickly. It is better as a short walk between rain bands than as a full morning out.

A warm, partly cloudy Wednesday suits a culture-first day across Centro and the Zona Sul.

The headline pick is free: the Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil, open today from 9am to 8pm.

Markets settled in a cautious mood on Tuesday, ahead of US inflation data.

Your day in one line: coffee in Centro, free art at CCBB, a late garden walk in Jardim Botânico, then a low-key Lapa evening.

SNAPSHOT

Slow the pace. Let the city reveal itself at room temperature.

03

What to See & Do

WEDNESDAY IN RIO

TODAY’S PICK — FREE CULTURE CCBB Centro then Real Gabinete: two free stops within a ten-minute walk Start at Centro Cultural Banco do Brasil on Rua Primeiro de Março. It opens at 9am and is free, with rotating exhibitions and a calm central atrium. Take the Metrô Line 1 or 2 to Uruguaiana and walk five minutes, or ride the VLT to Colombo. After an hour or two, walk to Real Gabinete Português de Leitura on Rua Luís de Camões. It is also free, but check its opening hours before you go. The reading room is the real draw: three floors of dark wood, stained glass and Portuguese literary history. For a late lunch, walk to Beco das Sardinhas near Praça XV for per-kilo restaurants around R$60 to R$75.

OUTDOORS — ESCAPE THE CENTRE Jardim Botânico opens at 11am on Wednesdays On Wednesdays the garden opens at 11am, so plan a late-afternoon visit after the heat eases. Entry is R$40 for residents and R$80 for foreigners, with the park staying open until 5pm. The imperial palms avenue and the orchid house give you a shaded, quiet reset away from the Centro crowds. Take the Metrô to Jardim Botânico and walk ten minutes to the main gate on Rua Jardim Botânico.

COFFEE & WHERE TO WORK — CENTRO Dial 30 in Centro or Curto Café for a desk-and-espresso morning Dial 30 serves quality coffee on Rua do Senado from early morning. Wi-Fi is reliable and seating settles down after 10am. Curto Café on Rua São José has faster service, good pão de queijo and a quieter corner for an hour of email catch-up. Both accept card and Pix; a flat white plus pastry runs about R$25 to R$32.

THE CONTRASTING PLAY — QUIET GARDENS Parque Lage at golden hour, free and walkable from the metro If the city feels heavy, skip the hilltop crowds and head to Parque Lage, which has no entry fee. The lawns and the Palacete facade are calmer in the last hour before sunset at 5:53pm. Combine it with a late lunch nearby in Jardim Botânico or Gávea, then walk back toward Lagoa for the sunset.

TONIGHT, AFTER 7 PM Lapa midweek: live samba at Rio Scenarium or a quieter drink at Bar do Omar Lapa works on a Wednesday without the Friday crush. Rio Scenarium on Rua do Lavradio has live samba from around 9pm. Entry is typically R$40 to R$60 depending on the programme; arrive by 8pm to avoid the queue. For a lower-key start, have a caipirinha at Bar do Omar around the corner, then decide if you want more noise. Take the Metrô to Cinelândia and walk twelve minutes, or use a ride app after dark.

ALSO ON TODAY Museu Nacional de Belas Artes — Centro — 10am to 6pm, free; partial reopening of Brazilian modern galleries Paço Imperial — Praça XV, Centro — midday to 6pm, free; colonial building with changing shows Theatro Municipal guided visit — Centro — guided visits on Wednesdays, R$20; check the box office for times Parque Natural Municipal da Catacumba — Lagoa — open until 5pm, free entry; short trail with lake views

04

Getting Around

TRANSPORT

Metrô Lines 1, 2 and 4 are running normally today. The single-journey fare is R$7.90, so a RioCard or contactless payment saves time if you make four or more trips.

The VLT light rail operates through Centro with connections to Santos Dumont airport. If late rain arrives, expect ride-app surge pricing in Centro between 6pm and 8pm.

05

Where to Eat

LUNCH & DINNER

Lunch: Beco das Sardinhas near Praça XV offers per-kilo lunch at R$60–75, while Dial 30 in Centro pairs coffee with a light toast and flat white for about R$30.

Dinner: For a quiet midweek dinner, Bar do Omar in Lapa serves good Brazilian comfort food around R$70–90 per person. In Laranjeiras, Belmonte offers chopp, pasteis and a lively but not chaotic Wednesday atmosphere.

06

Practical Info

GOOD TO KNOW

Carry a light cardigan for air-conditioned galleries and the metro. Use a crossbody bag in Centro and keep your phone close when photographing street scenes.

Cards and Pix are widely accepted, but keep R$50 in small notes for street snacks and tips.

After dark in Lapa, stay on main streets, avoid quiet lanes and use a ride app for door-to-door safety.

07

Community & Lifestyle

FOR NEWCOMERS

The Rio expat WhatsApp groups often post a midweek coffee at Curto Café in Centro; check the usual channels if you want company while you work.

Digital nomads without a fixed office often cluster at Dial 30 in Centro or the co-working spaces in Botafogo, which stay open on weekdays with day passes.

08

Game Day

THE WEEK AHEAD

Fluminense host Palmeiras tonight at the Maracanã in the first leg of their Copa Libertadores semi-final, with kick-off at 21:30.

Flamengo play Estudiantes in La Plata on Thursday, also at 21:30 Brasília time. On match days, Botafogo fans head to Boteco Belmonte in Botafogo.

Flamengo supporters use Bar Bracarense in Leblon, where the screen goes on from early afternoon on match days.

Kick-off for both matches is 21:30 Brasília time, which is 8:30 pm on the US East Coast.

09

Business & Markets

WEEK IN FIGURES

US markets ended Tuesday in a holding pattern, with the S&P 500 down 0.02% at 7,805. Investors are waiting for US inflation data to decide whether rate expectations need to shift.

The market mood is one of watchfulness rather than alarm. The Ibovespa fell 1.04% to 206,888, and the real lost 0.81% against the dollar.

For expats earning in dollars or euros, the quiet session means no fresh reason to change a remittance plan today. The more important signal arrives with the US inflation print later today.

10

Plan Ahead

THE WEEK

THE DAYS AHEAD THU 15 — Warmer and drier; good day for beach or a morning hike before work. FRI 16 — Hottest day of the week; pair morning outdoors with an air-conditioned museum afternoon. SAT 17 — Small rain chance; check club channels for any confirmed football fixture. SUN 18 — Beach flags and a long lunch; markets closed, no business flow. MON 19 — Back to full-service museums and a normal working week across the city.

Background: Rio de Janeiro Nightlife Tonight: Quiet Tuesday, Weekend Shows Ahead.

11

FAQ

QUICK ANSWERS

I only have one free day in Rio and want culture without spending much.

Use today’s free pair: CCBB in Centro and Real Gabinete Português de Leitura are both free and within a ten-minute walk of each other. CCBB is open 9am to 8pm; check Real Gabinete’s hours before you go.

Is it warm enough for the beach today, and is the sea safe?

The air is warm around 27°C, but the sea is about 22°C and waves are moderate. Swim between the flags at Copacabana or Ipanema. Avoid swimming at the far points where red flags are out in the afternoon.

How do I get around Centro safely and cheaply today?

Take the Metrô to Uruguaiana or Cinelândia; the single fare is R$7.90 and lines are running normally. The VLT light rail connects Centro landmarks and Santos Dumont airport. After dark, use a ride app for short hops in Lapa.

The Continent’s Mood Today

Latin America feels like a region waiting for two verdicts. One is the US inflation report due today, and the other is the Brazilian runoff on 25 October.

Currencies show the nerves: the Brazilian real, Mexican peso and Chilean peso all weakened on Tuesday, while the Colombian and Argentine pesos firmed. The mood is not panic, but a weary vigilance about what breaks next.

Argentina – A Fragile, Hard-Won Calm

The national statistics agency reported September inflation of 1.9%, in line with forecasts and a second straight month below 2%. Annual inflation was 33.4%.

The peso firmed 0.23% to 1,513 per dollar on Tuesday. For a foreigner, the heady days of panic seem paused, but prices are still rising by about a third a year.
